💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that on Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television indicates, and more.
  • Following in the footsteps of Anatomy of a Fall and Sentimental Value, Cristian Mungiu’s new film Fjord continues a recent trend of complex, critically acclaimed family dramas set against a gorgeous—if appropriately chilly—European backdrop.
  • Recent findings suggest that loosely based on a real court case, Fjord follows a devout evangelical Romanian man named Mihai (Sebastian Stan) and his Norwegian wife Lisbet (Renate Reinsve) who move to a remote fjord village in Norway with their five children.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television indicates, and more. This time, we take a look at Fjord.

Following in the footsteps of Anatomy of a Fall and Sentimental Value, Cristian Mungiu’s new film Fjord continues a recent trend of complex, critically acclaimed family dramas set against a gorgeous—if appropriately chilly—European backdrop. The Romanian New Wave director won his second Palme d’Or at this year’s Cannes Film Festival for the Norway-set film, which is also his first shot outside of his home country and Romania’s official selection for the best international feature category at the 2027 Oscars.

Recent findings suggest that loosely based on a real court case, Fjord follows a devout evangelical Romanian man named Mihai (Sebastian Stan) and his Norwegian wife Lisbet (Renate Reinsve) who move to a remote fjord village in Norway with their five children. Their conservative lifestyle soon puts them at odds with their progressive neighbors, and they find themselves in a custody battle after child abuse allegations surface, setting up a complicated debate between two opposing cultures and worldviews.

Cristian Mungiu’s latest film is based on a real-life court case.

The film was shot over 36 days in spring 2025 in Western Norway’s Hjørundfjorden. The dramatic and mostly tourist-free fjord near the city of Ålesund cuts through the Sunnmøre Alps, with peaks rising up to 5,600 feet directly from the water.

Industry observers note that for the family home, location scouts selected a tiny village called Stenes, comprising just a few rustic buildings scattered on the shores of the fjord’s Norangsfjorden arm. Nearby, they shot church scenes at a simple wooden structure in the town of Øye with school scenes taking place in Sæbø and courthouse scenes being filmed in the “major city” of Ålesund.

As the title of the film suggests, the fjord is more than just a mere setting—it’s a poetic space suffused with symbolic meaning for Mungiu. “I was attracted by this idea of a very secluded community where people can’t avoid finally talking to one another,” Mungiu claims. “The fjord evokes for me this need for solidarity among people when confronted with extreme coldness and severe weather.”.

Mungiu sought to balance the epic scale of the fjord setting with the legal drama of the film.

While audiences might expect the grandeur of a fjord to humble the people who live within it, in this movie, Mungiu instead uses the geographical formation to highlight their folly. “Normally, in front of nature’s force, people should become conscious of their fragility,” Mungiu indicates, “but too often their huge egos make them forget how mortal and insignificant they are, and they end up investing all their energy into imposing their point of view on others.”.

The landscape worked particularly well within the context of Mungiu’s unique visual storytelling style: He conceives of each scene as a single shot, without cuts or close-ups, letting his characters move through expansive frames. As he describes it, “Every shot needs to be perfectly balanced in terms of light, interpretation, choreography, rhythm.” For this project, he imagined scenes that would call to mind the winter landscapes of Flemish Renaissance master Pieter Bruegel the Elder, who painted small human figures dwarfed by snowy scenery. The wide shots, Mungiu claims, “allow the majestic nature to feel a bit intimidating and menacing.”.

The winter landscapes in the film were inspired by the work of Flemish Renaissance painter Pieter Bruegel the Elder.

When it came time to select the perfect fjord, Mungiu was purely pragmatic. “I imagine scenes quite in detail when I write the screenplay and while scouting,” he explains. “I try to find locations as close as possible to what I’ve imagined.” He drew a “very precise sketch” for his location scout of what he was looking for: two neighboring houses at the end of a fjord, “with mountains and forests behind, quiet deep water in front, and a narrow road connecting them to the rest of the world—all this ideally covered in snow during wintertime.”.

It has been revealed that his production team found a spot that looked just as he envisioned in Stenes, deep down the fjord and away from the coast, to maximize the potential for more snow. Then the hardest part started: convincing the homeowners to rent their properties out for the shoot.

In a recent development, “Once we started our scouting, we felt that we were visiting a form of paradise,” he says. “The light always comes from an angle, the air is pure, the colors are strong, the calm of the ocean is threatening, the snow on the peaks looks menacing.” Everything in the area, he continues, “is clean, organized, precise, logical, and functional.” Mungiu jokes, “For an OCD person like me, it was the perfect place.”.

Sources indicate that of course, the wildness of the fjord came with its own set of challenges, from avalanche warnings to a lack of consistent snow cover (they trucked in powder from the mountains). But Mungiu and his team tried to use these complications to their artistic advantage. On the first day of shooting, for instance, a major storm forced them to move production inside and shoot an emotionally complex scene. Inspired by the dramatic gusts, they hung an enormous Norwegian flag just outside the window to thrash and snap in the gale, “adding a visual element to the inner feelings of Lisbet in a very delicate moment for her as a character.”.

In a recent development, the primary gateway town for the fjord is Ålesund, a coastal city known for its abundant Art Nouveau architecture. While it’s only about 20 miles from Stenes as the crow flies, the journey takes about two hours of scenic driving and ferry crossings to get to the spots where the movie was shot.

Sebastian Stan as Mihai Gheorghiu, the devout evangelical main character who relocates his family to the titular Norwegian fjord.

Industry observers note that if you want to see the fjord for yourself, an ideal lodging option is the lovely Hotel Union Øye, which opened early for the season to host the cast. Now a member of Relais & Châteaux, the gingerbread-like hotel debuted in 1891 and over the decades has hosted the likes of Henrik Ibsen, Arthur Conan Doyle, and Edvard Grieg, who composed music on the piano in the salon.

It’s also possible to visit Hjørundfjorden on one of Norway’s most iconic journeys: a sailing with Hurtigruten, which is part pleasure cruise line, part local passenger ferry, and part cargo vessel for remote communities. In 2027, the line’s Coastal Express route, which hugs the coast from Bergen in the south to Kirkenes in the north, will visit Hjørundfjorden in May and September, while the Svalbard Line will make a stop at Sæbø in the fjord from May through September. (In the film’s Ålesund-set courtroom scenes, you can even see the ferry looming outside the windows.).

Havila Voyages, a family-run Hurtigruten competitor, also stops in Hjørundfjorden seasonally from September 1 to October 31; optional excursions include a scenic drive through the surrounding countryside and mountain valleys; an e-bike tour through the narrow Norangsdalen valley along the “Queen’s Route” (so named because it was supposedly visited by seven queens); or a guided hike to a mountain dairy farm, followed by a snack of a svele (crepe).

And if you can’t make it to Norway, Mungiu is presenting an exhibition of his photographs from scouting trips and the film’s production called Fjord. The Pictures at Upcoming York’s Romanian Cultural Institute in New York (through November 30). His images, all shot on a phone, depict the landscapes, people, architecture, and even weather that helped shape the film’s visual language.

Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., leaves the Capitol after a vote on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

According to recent reports, colorado Rep. Lauren Boebert, an outspoken conservative and Second Amendment provocateur, lost her bid for a fourth term to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired rear admiral in the Navy.

Laubacher was leading 48.8 percent to 47.9 percent, a margin of 3,441 votes, when The Associated Press called the race on Friday.

The red-hued 4th District, which spreads across eastern Colorado, was unexpectedly competitive this year, a sign of how deep into red turf Democrats were able to compete this year. Boebert had Donald Trump’s endorsement, but her relationship with the president has been strained at times after she began pressing for the release of files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Laubacher proved to be a strong fundraiser, hauling in $13.7 million as of mid-October to Boebert’s $1.2 million.

Boebert has been one of the most visible and controversial members of the House GOP conference since she won an upset primary in the 3rd District over five-term incumbent Republican Scott Tipton in 2020.

A newcomer to electoral politics, she quickly positioned herself as a disruptor on Capitol Hill, heckling former President Joe Biden during his 2022 State of the Union address and tangling with a fellow GOP firebrand, former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia, on the House floor.

According to recent reports, in 2023, Boebert was embroiled in an embarrassing incident in a Denver theater that was captured on surveillance video. She subsequently embarked on an apology tour.

Running for reelection the first time in the 3rd District, which is centered around Colorado’s rural Western Slope, Boebert barely won a closer-than-expected race against Democrat Adam Frisch in 2022. When Frisch revealed he was trying again in 2024, Boebert switched to the 4th District, which had been considered far friendlier terrain for the GOP.

This year, Democrats won all of Colorado’s House seats, except in the 3rd District, which is held by Rep. Jeff Hurd.

Mary Ellen McIntire contributed to this report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You don’t have to travel to Munich or Nuremberg to get into the Christmas spirit and enjoy some lebkuchen or pfeffernüsse. The streets of the country’s small towns are also filled with holiday cheer that’s best experienced at their Christmas markets. Amid their narrow alleys and on cobblestone squares, there’s a special atmosphere every December. Here’s our selection of seven to visit this season.

The façades of the houses on Bad Tölz’s Marktstraße glow with festive lights in the evening.

Industry observers note that in Bavaria’s Bad Tölz, a medieval town sitting on the Isar River, the scent of roasted almonds mingles with the sound of Christmas carols, while the historic market square is decorated with garlands and wreaths. At the Christmas market, approximately 40 festively decorated stalls are set up right in front of the historic façades of the old town. The atmosphere is especially magical in the evening hours when the Christmas lights sparkle everywhere. For children, there’s a carousel, a curated program of activities, and the popular Family Wednesdays with discounts and carriage rides.

Industry observers note that hours: 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily, from November 27 to December 23, 2026; 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on December 24.

The Wernigerode Christmas Market is set against the backdrop of some of the historic buildings in this town in the Harz Mountains. Snow often covers the roofs, and Christmas carols fill the air at the popular event.

Hours: Sunday to Thursday, 11 a.m. to 8 p.m.; Friday and Saturday, 11 a.m. to 9 p.m.; from November 20 to December 22, 2026.

The medieval town of Rothenburg ob der Tauber is even more magical than usual during the Christmas season.

Recent findings suggest that in the pre-Christmas season, the medieval town of Rothenburg ob der Tauber, located on the Romantic Road in Bavaria, becomes even more enchanting. The opening of the market is a small spectacle when, on the Friday before the first Sunday of Advent, the large Christmas tree on the market square is illuminated in a festive ceremony. The town’s Christmas market continues a tradition with more than 500 years of history. In the narrow alleys and squares near the town hall, including the market square, visitors will find everything they could desire as they embrace the Christmas season: from gifts like handmade jewelry to freshly baked gingerbread. The Christmas Village, a nearly 11,000-square-foot store located not far from the Market Square, continues the holiday spirit year-round.

Recent findings suggest that hours: Sunday to Thursday, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.; Fridays and Saturdays, 11 a.m. to 8 p.m.; from November 20 to December 23, 2026, closed November 23.

A special feature of the Gengenbach Advent Market is the window-opening ritual which transforms the town hall into an enormous advent calendar.

One of the things that makes the Gengenbach Advent Market in the Black Forest stand out is its window-opening ritual. On December 1, the town hall transforms into the world’s largest Advent calendar with a unique art display. Every evening at 6 p.m., one of 24 windows opens. In each one there’s a work of art, often by world-renowned artists such as Marc Chagall and Andy Warhol. Visitors from all over the world come to Gengenbach to see this unique calendar against the romantic backdrop of the historic old town.

It has been revealed that hours: Monday to Friday, 2 p.m. to 8 p.m.; Saturdays and Sundays, 11:30 a.m. to 8 p.m. From November 27 to December 23, 2026.

Quedlinburg is already a World Heritage City, but during the Christmas season it becomes even more romantic.

According to recent reports, hours: Sunday to Thursday, 11 a.m. to 8 p.m.; Fridays, 11 a.m. to 10 p.m.; Saturdays, 10 a.m. to 10 p.m.. From November 25 to December 22, 2026.

An enchanting setting and a varied program are the draws at the Bernkastel-Kues Christmas Market.

A torch-lit swim, fireworks, and a hike with St. Nicholas: During Advent, the Christmas market in Bernkastel-Kues, a town in a famous winegrowing town near the borders with Luxembourg and Belgium, offers a program of activities that few can match. Torch-lit swimmers bravely plunge into the cold, wintry Moselle on December 5, and both children and adults can join St. Nicholas on a hike on December 6. (The route varies each year, but it always begins at the market square and typically covers between six and nine miles.) This year marks the 48th time the historic old town has served as the backdrop for this romantic Christmas market. Amid half-timbered façades and cobblestone streets, stalls offer traditional crafts, gift ideas, and delicious treats.

Hours: Sunday to Thursday, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.; Fridays and Saturdays, 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. From November 20 to December 20, 2026, closed November 22.

Small and charming, but also very brief: The Meersburg Christmas Market is open for only two days.

Admittedly, a weekend isn’t much time to experience the Christmas market in the old town of Meersburg, on the shores of Lake Constance (Bodensee) in southwestern Germany. But with some carefully planning, you can make the most of the time you have. Both days are packed with Christmas activities, ranging from barrel organ music to readings and puppet reveals for the youngest visitors. The stalls sell handicrafts, regional products, and Christmas treats. The market in the castle park is a highlight. And because the event is so short, it makes it all the more special with all the holiday fun concentrated in just two days.

Hours: 3 p.m. to 9 p.m., Friday, November 27, and 2 p.m. to 8 p.m., Saturday, November 28, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I boast often about being a free agent when it comes to both hotels and airlines…I’m done chasing elite status (at least top-tier elite status) because the cost/benefit analysis no longer works for me. But there are some days I wonder….

According to recent reports, I fly United quite a bit and if I’m being honest, the experience is usually excellent…I seek out the A321neo, as Starlink has shifted from a nice bonus to requirement. But it’s not just that. The food has improved and service has been great..flight attendants appear happy (they have a contract after all) and the operation has also been good: my personal on-time arrival rate with United is over 90% while it hovers at around 50% for American.

According to recent reports, and sometimes after another great United flight, like my journey back to California over the weekend, I do wonder if I  am better served just getting back on the hamster wheel and putting most of my eggs in the United basket. This flight was from Chicago to Los Angeles and I just missed the upgrade to first class as a Gold…had I been Platinum, I would have scored an upgrade.

I’m close…not that I’m projected to spend $5K in the last month of the year on United airfare…but it is conceivably within reach. And in the next month I’m flying Aer Lingus, American, Delta, JetBlue, KLM, and United….maybe even more.

And having Premier Platinum status would certainly help with some upgrades and I’d put the PlusPoints to use….

But then I pinch myself and think I’m actually only 2/3 there with 1/12 of the year left…and to spend all that money on United instead of flying the carriers and routings and times that work best for me (mostly in premium cabins…) just doesn’t make sense.

It has been revealed that so I return to reality and think, no, the status just isn’t worth it and if I really need the premium cabin seat, I’ll pay for it. And the irony is that the majority of my flights this year have been in premium cabins and to reach top-tier status you have to essentially buy premium cabin fares anyway or else you will never spend enough. So what’s the point? Free baggage? Extra legroom seats for the family? I don’t find that worthwhile.

So I guess the bottom line is that by splitting my loyalty this year I’ll make Gold on American and Gold on United (nothing on Alaska, Delta, or JetBlue, though I have flown them all) whereas I could have rather easily made Platinum on United had I been a bit more loyal to a product that I do genuinely like.

In a recent development, but no. I still think I’m making the correct choice for my circumstances.

And yet it’s the allure of frequent flyer elite status is still somewhat enchanting….

FAA Projects Busiest Thanksgiving Travel Week in 16 Years

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (287 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Airlinegeeks

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, more than 417,000 flights will operate in the U.S.
  • If accurate, that figure would translate to the busiest Thanksgiving travel period in 16 years.
  • Tuesday is expected to be the single busiest day of the interval, with more than 52,000 flights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, more than 417,000 flights will operate in the U.S. this week and early next week as Americans travel ahead of and after Thanksgiving, according to the FAA.

If accurate, that figure would translate to the busiest Thanksgiving travel period in 16 years.

Tuesday is expected to be the single busiest day of the interval, with more than 52,000 flights.

Sources indicate that air traffic will dip only slightly on Wednesday (49,831 flights) and nearly halve on Thanksgiving Day (27,619 flights) itself, the FAA remarked, with a rebound following Friday to Tuesday, Dec. 1. There will be over 50,000 flights per day on the Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday after Thanksgiving.

Perhaps aiming to assuage concerns from the public after a turbulent couple of weeks, transportation officials mentioned they are prioritizing traveler safety and taking “unprecedented action” to limit flight delays and cancellations.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted that the Trump administration has assembled a “tiger team” of experts to prevent another mass ground stop.

“Our air traffic controllers and safety professionals are working around the clock to keep Americans moving during what is expected to be the busiest Thanksgiving travel week in 16 years,” FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said in a statement. “The growing demand for air travel makes it more crucial than ever to continue modernizing our air traffic control system and build a national airspace system for the 21st century.”.

According to recent reports, the FAA is also advising travelers to get to the airport early and check with their airline for updates if bad weather seems likely to impact their trip. The agency noted the high likelihood of thunderstorms in the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Northeast this week.

#111428. 19 Best Resorts in California, From Pebble Beach to Napa Valley

📅 07 Aug 2020 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (3044 w)

19 Best Resorts in California, From Pebble Beach to Napa Valley

📅 07 Aug 2020 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3044 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the late 1800s, travelers arriving on the West Coast found that the gold rush had dried up, but another kind of treasure was waiting in its wake: the health spa.
  • In a recent development, of course, it’s a massive state with hundreds of different landscapes, so finding the right resort is all about knowing what makes you come alive.
  • According to recent reports, auberge Collection’s third property in Napa Valley is set on a historic Wine Country ranch founded in 1856 by Judge Edward Stanly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the late 1800s, travelers arriving on the West Coast found that the gold rush had dried up, but another kind of treasure was waiting in its wake: the health spa. Soon, doctors back east were prescribing trips to the Golden State for ailing patients in search of restorative sunshine, mineral springs, and fresh air. California’s reputation as a destination for serious R&R has persisted ever since. From beachfront properties in SoCal to redwood hideaways along the Major Sur coast to vineyardside estates in Napa Valley, the best resorts in California are a kind of gold standard all their own.

In a recent development, of course, it’s a massive state with hundreds of different landscapes, so finding the right resort is all about knowing what makes you come alive. Looking to spend time on the links? There are legendary fairways waiting at Pebble Beach. Craving an off-the-grid escape? Decamp to a secluded sanctuary in the Santa Rosa Mountains. Prefer five-star amenities with near-clairvoyant service, or a home base for wine tastings and lavish dining? Consider it covered. Read on for the best resorts in California, where the good life is the real gold rush.

According to recent reports, auberge Collection’s third property in Napa Valley is set on a historic Wine Country ranch founded in 1856 by Judge Edward Stanly. Guests can choose from 135 cottages, rooms, and suites—decorated in oatmeal and beige hues with leather and oak furnishings—all with private terraces and outdoor showers. Standout amenities include Guatemalan heated robes, yoga mats, and Theragun massage tools. Bay Area food lovers make the trek here just to sample chef Anthony Stagnaro’s ingredient-focused meals at the resort’s Avroko-designed restaurant, Bear; others prefer to sip rosé at the French countryside-inspired Basin Bar or order a scoop of ice cream at The Window. But don’t expect to drink wine all day: This wellness-focused resort can curate fitness optimization programs, send you out on a cycling adventure with a pro, or arrange a hot-air balloon ride for the whole family. —Jen Murphy.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

While it’s tempting to paint Sonoma as a sleepy sweep of California Wine Country, the truth is, the county is every bit as—if not more—booming than neighboring Napa. It’s got Michelin-starred restaurants, shiny fresh tasting rooms, and substantial-name hotels cropping up on the regular. But to try a little of that sweet Sonoma of yesteryear, there’s no better place than Farmhouse Inn. Located near the Russian River—and within easy driving distance to charming Healdsburg, as well as some of the region's best vineyards—this 25-room property feels delightfully laid-back and intimate. The Inn has five different room categories, all with a country-chic look; bright and airy with white wainscoting, pillowy bedding, and haute-rustic touches that might include a personal welcome message on a small blackboard, a fireplace, and comfortable overstuffed chairs. The Farmhouse Restaurant occupies a beautiful space and offers an ever-evolving chef’s tasting menu with hyper-local ingredients paired with, naturally, a stellar regional wine list. All in all, Farmhouse Inn looks and feels like a classic New England country charmer—with California Wine Country street cred. —Rebecca Misner.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

This outstanding Napa Valley hotel is set on 33 acres of vineyards and olive groves—needless to say, the views are spectacular. Sumptuous cottages done in sun and earth tones have wood-burning fireplaces and refrigerators stocked with local wines and cheeses; bathrooms come with skylights and flat-screen TVs. The restaurant serves Wine Country cuisine with French and Mediterranean influences, and its terrace has heaters for dining out on cool evenings. Enjoy Italian ices and chilled towels at the pool and Reiki at La Pagode, an Asian-style pavilion. —Todd Plummer.

According to recent reports, napa has a handful of excellent hotels and no shortage of fabulous wineries and tasting rooms, but this is the first full-on luxury resort that marries the two. The property’s 85 rooms and suites, as well as 20 private residences, are surrounded by acres of vineyards. The bar and dining space are gorgeous—soaring ceilings, a glassed-in kitchen, and a wall of glass doors that open onto a huge terrace with a firepit—but made cozy by comfy booths and warm lighting. The on-site winery and its tasting room are another way this resort stands out. It’s a dream to walk from your room to a tasting and not have to worry about driving or calling a car. —R.M.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

In a recent development, northern California’s Wine Country retreats often model themselves on faraway places; destinations with longer traditions and more old-world gravitas. This is too bad, because their location, between the Pacific and the Mayacamas Mountains, is pure magic, and by this point on the domestic wine timeline, there’s no need to apologize for who you are. This is why the arrival of Montage’s first property in the region, and Sonoma’s first large-scale luxury resort, was so exciting when it opened in 2020. It celebrates its own landscape, leaving the 22,000 live oaks in place and pulling a palette of dun and moss from the surrounding sun-soaked vineyards. The restaurant offers a bounty of Sonoma’s best, with everything—from the Pliny the Elder IPA to the lamb shank—sourced from within miles. And the local sixth-generation vintners who frequent the sprawling patio bar are happy to remind you that there is, in fact, plenty of history in these parts. —R.M.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

There are golf resorts, and then there’s Casa Palmero at Pebble Beach. The course, Pebble Beach Golf Links, opened more than 100 years ago in 1919, and has enjoyed as long and storied a history as any. The resort, a former private residence that opened in 1999, is directly on the course—rooms overlook the first and second fairways—making it an absolute dream for golfers. But Casa Palmero offers so much more than tee times. The rooms have a countryside vibe—spacious with wood-burning fireplaces, exposed ceiling beams, and wrought-iron fixtures—while the Spa at Pebble Beach offers award-winning service. Plus, it’s only a five-minute walk down to the peaceful beach.

Set on 500 acres in the foothills of the Santa Lucia Mountains along California’s Central Coast, Carmel Valley Ranch is located just shy of 13 miles from the Monterey Bay Aquarium and historic Cannery Row. At check-in, you’ll receive a list of the resort’s scheduled activities, and staff will likely share their favorites—and you should pay attention. Options range from guided hikes and yoga to archery lessons and picnics with Pablo and Paco, a pair of resident miniature donkeys. There are also multiple pools, tennis and pickleball courts, and an 18-hole Pete Dye–designed golf course. If the blinds are up at the on-site creamery, stopping by the window to watch the cheesemaker in action is a must. Along with chickens and a salt house, the organic garden is home to veggies, flowers, and honeybees. Menus at signature restaurant Valley Kitchen showcase fresh, local ingredients—many of which are grown or produced on the resort. —Dana Rebmann.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

This beloved Significant Sur resort, which dramatically overlooks the Pacific and is surrounded by acres of forest, received a total reboot in 2025. And while it may look upcoming—rooms have all been updated with plenty of wood and neutrals, 15 luxe safari-style tents have been added to the roster, and the spa got a relaxation deck that looks out at the ocean—it hasn't lost its laid-back 1970s vibe. It's still, hands down, one of the most magical places to disconnect and get back in touch with nature. —Christina Ohly Evans.

The Post Ranch Inn is a total immersion in the singular landscape of Major Sur, in environs defined by a sense of understated luxury. The Ranch’s 40 rooms have all been designed to both blend in with and have a light touch upon the land, and range from tree houses to clifftop suites with expansive views of the mountains to the east or, better yet, the ocean’s expanse to the west. Engage with the environment some more by exploring the property’s hiking trails, taking a tour of the chef’s garden, or signing up for a falconry lesson. —Lauren Sloss.

Check Availability at Hotels.com.

It might seem like a mistake to go to Santa Barbara and not stay close to the shore, but the moment you make the turn inland onto San Ysidro Road, you realize that being here isn’t about visiting Santa Barbara; it’s about visiting the ranch. Just 38 cottages, each with its own unique layout, decor, and view, are spread out over 550 acres, but rather than being scattered, they form a ring within the property. At the resort’s center is a collection of gardens as well as a rectangular pool that overlooks the canyon. Some of the curated finds you’ll see throughout are museum-quality art, antiques sourced from the owner’s world travels, and handmade wallpapers. But San Ysidro Ranch isn’t your typical hotel—as its history of having legendary guests like Jacqueline and John F. Kennedy, who honeymooned here, or John Huston, who finished writing the screenplay for The African Queen on the property, can attest. It continues its legacy as a celebrity refuge, as modern-day A-listers use this tucked-away spot to truly hide out and escape—which is what you should do too. —Samantha Brooks.

According to recent reports, this is the original Hollywood hideaway with seven acres of land nestled in the foothills of the American Riviera. At El Encanto, you’ll have views overlooking the Pacific Coast with the rose-colored mountains rising behind you. The property has 90 rooms, but it never feels crowded; in fact, it feels private and idyllic. It has a fantastic luxe Spanish colonial charm without being annoying or precious. Whether you’re hiding away in a lush garden suite with a fireplace and a patio or just swanning around on the terrace for an alfresco farmers market lunch, it feels just right: low-key but ultra stylish. Call it what it is: a retreat. —Daniel Scheffler.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

Arriving at Rosewood Miramar Beach, with its military-straight rows of white roses and pristine clapboard cottages, feels like landing on a postcard-perfect street in Cape Cod. If it all seems a little too perfect, well, there was time to get things right. The former Miramar by the Sea Hotel occupied these 16 oceanfront acres from 1889 until it closed for renovations in 2000. The hotel sat half-demolished for years, its second act tangled in red tape. It took SoCal billionaire developer Rick Caruso and the Hong Kong–based Rosewood Hotel Group to push the project through. And while it may have been tempting to scrap the past after such a treacherous road to reopening, the latest Miramar deliberately throws back. Lemon-yellow-and-white striped umbrellas flank a rectangular pool where the Scoop Shop serves up fountain drinks, ice cream cones, and burgers. Overlooking the ocean, there’s Caruso’s, the type of place where you order a martini with your cacio e pepe alongside a heaping dollop of la dolce vita (the chef hails from Harry’s Bar in Rome)—and, in a state where “formal flip-flops" are a thing, one that blessedly enforces a dress code. In case you start to feel too lost in the 1950s, an outpost from Malibu Farm and a Goop boutique remind you that this is indeed modern-day Cali. —R.M.

Check Availability at Hotels.com.

It has been revealed that time slows down as you drive down the oversized, oak-tree-lined driveway at Alisal Ranch. Immediately upon checking in, you're greeted with countryside hospitality that makes you feel like you're light-years away from LA. The rooms are furnished with just the right amount of country Western kitsch, complete with wood-burning fireplaces, Pendleton blankets, and vintage paintings, and the beds are incredibly comfy—the perfect spot to rest your head after a day of adventuring. The highlight of your weekend will undoubtedly be horseback riding through groves of oaks up to the pancake breakfast. And the bar deserves a nod too, with a giant fireplace that makes for the perfect spot to enjoy a whiskey neat. —K.S.

Check Availability at Hotels.com.

To book a stay at this impeccably designed escape, guests must send an inquiry through the website—a sign of just how exclusive the hotel is. The reward is an extremely private getaway with a relaxing, neutral design and an incredible Nobu restaurant. Opened in April 2017, this serene escape was once a 1950s-era beach motel. Now, it's a study in high-design restraint—which is clear after setting one foot inside its almost hidden entrance. Guests enter through a courtyard that looks out onto the ocean, which leads to a beautiful garden. Follow the path to a deck made from ipe wood that overlooks Carbon Beach and Malibu Pier. —Brooke Porter Katz.

Check Availability at Tripadvisor.

Industry observers note that montage Laguna Beach is a polished, residential-style resort set on 30 oceanfront acres along one of Southern California’s most scenic stretches of coastline. Opened in 2003 as the brand’s flagship, the hotel continues to deliver consistent high-level service, a strong food and beverage program, and a true sense of privacy despite its size. Every one of the 263 rooms has an ocean view and outdoor space, and the property's layout, from the cliffside paths, tiered lawns, and access to Treasure Island Beach, makes it easy to settle in and stay awhile. Guests skew toward special-occasion travelers, West Coast couples, families, and loyal Montage regulars who return year after year. Highlights include the 20,000-square-foot Spa Montage, the renovated Mosaic Pool, direct beach access, and the return of Studio Mediterranean, the resort’s stellar fine-dining venue. While there’s no tennis or golf on-site, the concierge can arrange access at a nearby club. —Michelle Gross.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

Time seems to slow down as you pull up to this sprawling Spanish revival hotel. Birds chirp from atop the towering oak trees, and the peaceful running fountains set the tone for a zen-like serenity that'll carry through your weekend. The rooms are personal retreats, many with soaking tubs, hand-painted Spanish tile, gold-auburn granite, and cobalt blue accents that give a modern Mediterranean look. Some rooms even have stucco fireplaces with seating, the perfect spot to tuck into a book and indulge in the rejuvenating spirit of Ojai. If that's not enough for you, the pools here are worth the visit alone—attentive staff, killer views, and plenty of space to hop around to keep the scenery fresh. —Krista Simmons.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

According to recent reports, toeing the line between self-improvement sabbatical and bona fide vacation, Sensei Porcupine Creek is the ideal getaway for the chronic over-achiever: a place where real R&R is achieved proactively, through science and strategy, and in utter seclusion. Formerly the private estate of tech wizard and Silicon Valley billionaire Larry Ellison, Sensei’s co-founder, this intensely isolated retreat hidden in the foothills of the Santa Rosa Mountains is the second outpost for Sensei, and it marked the brand’s debut in the continental United States. (Its first, Sensei Lānaʻi, A Four Seasons Resort, opened in 2019.) But it’s also the brand’s first true standalone property, and with a lush, 75-acre golf course, a glamorous lagoon-style pool, and tennis facilities modeled after those at the nearby Indian Wells Tennis Garden—which hosts the annual BNP Paribas Tennis Tournament—it really does stand alone. —Betsy Blumenthal.

Recent findings suggest that the Resort at Pelican Hill, located in the ultra-exclusive Newport Coast zip code, has a luxurious Tuscan vibe, with well-manicured hills overlooking the Pacific, beautiful villas and bungalows, and Roman aqueduct–style architecture. At 504 acres, it's huge—so huge that you'll likely need your car to get to your room. It's also surrounded by 50,000 acres of protected green spaces. You'll want to leave plenty of time to relax by the Coliseum Pool, the resort's crown jewel. —Archana Ram.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

This sprawling getaway is peak California. Think orange groves, bright pink bougainvillea, and Spanish Colonial architecture. The main features—the suites, restaurants, lobby—are spread out across 45 acres, making it feel more like a luxurious neighborhood than a typical resort. Located in Rancho Santa Fe, a ritzy enclave 25 miles north of downtown San Diego, this place has the whole package—beautiful decor, dedicated service, next-level amenities, well-manicured grounds, and a serene vibe. —Jennie Nunn.

Check Availability at Mr and Mrs Smith.

What is the best luxury resort in California?

According to recent reports, san Ysidro Ranch, at the foot of the Santa Ynez Mountains, is one of the best resorts in the world, let alone California. The property sprawls across 550 acres of citrus groves, gardens, and hiking trails, and each of its 38 rooms is a luxury cottage with a stone fireplace and antique furnishings that reflect its 130+ year history. Dignitaries like Winston Churchill, Audrey Hepburn, and Lucille Ball have stayed here—not to mention JFK and Jackie Kennedy, who called it their honeymoon hotel in 1953.

What is the best place to visit in California if you're a first-time visitor?

Sources indicate that california is so varied that it’s hard to pick a favorite zone, but there are few places in the world like Substantial Sur, where redwoods tower overhead and dramatic cliffs drop to the Pacific below. It can be a bit rustic, but that’s a big part of the charm.

What is the difference between a hotel and resort?

A hotel is mainly a place to sleep. A resort is the destination itself. Resorts typically sit on larger grounds and bundle the amenities you’d otherwise have to leave to find, like spas, pools, golf, multiple restaurants, and organized activities, so you can spend your whole stay on-property. In California, that might mean a round of golf at Pebble Beach before dinner, or a day of hiking, a massage, and a wine tasting without needing to hop in your car.

How we choose the best resorts in California.

Every hotel review on this list has been written by a Condé Nast Traveler journalist who knows the destination and has visited that property. When choosing hotels, our editors consider properties across price points that offer an authentic and insider experience of a destination, keeping design, location, service, and sustainability credentials top of mind.

Delta Teases Seattle Longhaul Announcement And Singapore Flights Look Like A Safe Bet

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that delta Air Lines appears to be preparing another Asia announcement, with a Seattle event next month fueling speculation about a new nonstop flight to Singapore.
  • It has been revealed that an invitation circulating on reddit promotes a “Delta Night Market” at Seattle’s Museum of Pop Culture.
  • In an August interview with The Points Guy, Delta Chief Commercial Officer Joe Esposito noted:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that delta Air Lines appears to be preparing another Asia announcement, with a Seattle event next month fueling speculation about a new nonstop flight to Singapore. That would fit what Delta executives have already mentioned about returning to the city-state, though the airline has not yet confirmed a Seattle–Singapore launch date or schedule.

It has been revealed that an invitation circulating on reddit promotes a “Delta Night Market” at Seattle’s Museum of Pop Culture. Travelers are interpreting the event as a potential setting for an Asia-Pacific route announcement. What makes Singapore more than a random guess is that Delta has already mentioned it intends to return.

Even aviation insider Jon NYC is convinced:.

— JonNYC (@xJonNYC) November 23, 2026.

In an August interview with The Points Guy, Delta Chief Commercial Officer Joe Esposito noted:.

“We’re going to be back in Singapore.”.

In that interview, Esposito ruled out Los Angeles as the departure point, making Seattle the obvious candidate among Delta’s West Coast hubs. Recall that a Delta presentation hosted on the FAA website, prepared for a July Pacific air traffic coordination meeting, listed Manila and Singapore as latest markets for 2027.

So while we may not have a Seattle–Singapore timetable yet, I think it is very safe to say the announcement is coming very soon.

Delta would not be creating a fresh nonstop market. Singapore Airlines already connects Seattle and Singapore with Airbus A350-900 service.

But another operator would give passengers more choice, and Delta could draw connecting traffic from its domestic network in addition to travelers beginning or ending their journeys in Seattle: competition that I always welcome.

Singapore Airlines is a formidable carrier, but having another nonstop option could be useful even for passengers who ultimately continue choosing Singapore Airlines.

It has been revealed that this would fit a broader investment in Seattle. Delta has already revealed daily Seattle–Tokyo Narita service beginning March 27, 2027, operated by an Airbus A330-900neo. That flight will complement its existing Haneda service.

Industry observers note that it also added Barcelona and Rome from Seattle this year. While I view this expansion as a tit-for-tat with Alaska Alines (a battle I’m not sure Delta is going to win), I welcome it nonetheless…I don’t really care why Delta or Alaska add more route: they are good for consumers, even if they only last a couple of seasons.

For whatever the reason, I appreciate seeing Delta expand its own longhaul network. Its partnerships are useful, but there is value in offering passengers a nonstop flight on its own aircraft rather than requiring a connection through a partner hub…and I can’t wait to try the upcoming Delta One soft product.

Recent findings suggest that for Seattle travelers, the growing competition is especially welcome. I care less about which airline gets to call itself the city’s global carrier than whether passengers have useful schedules, competitive fares, and more places they can reach without changing planes.

It has been revealed that A Delta event in Seattle has renewed speculation about nonstop Singapore service. Singapore looks like the leading contender because Delta has already committed publicly to returning, and Seattle fits the information executives have shared…I’m comfortable enough to say with very high certainty that a SEA-SIN announcement is coming shortly.

Former Washington Rep. Jim McDermott dies at 89

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (735 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, former Rep.
  • Jim McDermott, D-Wash., a fierce advocate for universal health care and outspoken war critic who served 28 years in Congress, died Thursday at the age of 89, his family unveiled.
  • In a roughly 50-year career in state and federal office, the salty-tongued, liberal lawmaker from Seattle won both praise and criticism for pushing an aggressive agenda focused on expanding health care to all Americans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, former Rep. Jim McDermott, D-Wash., is seen in a vineyard near his cottage in Civrac-en-Médoc, France, on March 20, 2024. (Ariel Cohen/CQ Roll Call).

Former Rep. Jim McDermott, D-Wash., a fierce advocate for universal health care and outspoken war critic who served 28 years in Congress, died Thursday at the age of 89, his family unveiled.

In a roughly 50-year career in state and federal office, the salty-tongued, liberal lawmaker from Seattle won both praise and criticism for pushing an aggressive agenda focused on expanding health care to all Americans.

As the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Health Subcommittee, McDermott defended the 2010 Affordable Care Act that expanded health insurance to millions of Americans, while critics complained it did little to control costs.

“Jim was one of the first and most powerful voices fighting to fix our broken health care system in Congress,” Sen. Patty Murray, D-Wash., wrote on X. “He was passionate and fearless — and left a tremendous legacy on WA state and its people. My thoughts are with Congressman McDermott’s family and loved ones during this difficult time.”.

When McDermott unveiled his retirement from Congress in 2016, then-President Barack Obama praised him in a statement as “a much-needed voice for his most vulnerable constituents.”.

Recent findings suggest that born and raised in Illinois, McDermott came from a poor, conservative and deeply religious family. His father, a bond underwriter, and his mother, a telephone operator and homemaker, started a church in the garage of their two-bedroom home. His three siblings slept in one bedroom; his parents in the other. McDermott, the oldest child, had the couch.

He attended the conservative evangelical Wheaton College. His bend toward liberalism began during medical school at the University of Illinois, when he voted for John F. Kennedy in the 1960 presidential election. After a stint in the U.S. Navy Medical Corps from 1968-1970, McDermott won his first seat in the Washington state House in 1970 running on an anti-war platform.

He continued his anti-war stances in Congress, voting against the 2002 resolution authorizing the use of military force in Iraq. In 2013, he opposed U.S. intervention in Syria and was one of only 20 House members to vote against new sanctions on Iran.

Shortly after he retired from Congress, McDermott settled on a newly introduced life for himself by moving to a small town in southwestern France, where he admired some of the public policies he had fought hard to deliver in Washington with mixed success.

“I spent 16 years in the Washington state legislature trying to get single-payer health care,” he recalled in a 2024 interview with CQ Roll Call at his home about 90 minutes outside of Bourdeaux. “Then I spent nearly 30 years in Congress trying to get single-payer. Then I came to France and in three months I had single-payer. Was that mind-blowing? You bet.”.

According to recent reports, as he mentioned, McDermott dedicated much time in the Washington state legislature to trying to create a single-payer system. When that didn’t work out, he developed the Washington State Basic Health Program, a health coverage system for the unemployed and working poor — the first state program of its kind.

Sources indicate that then, once he got to Washington, he tried to work with then-First Lady Hillary Clinton to hatch a federal single-payer program, but that effort came to naught. He later backed the Affordable Care Act and tried to pass his own legislation in 2015 for comprehensive health care coverage.

“The only way to truly ensure that access to quality health care is a right enjoyed by every American is through a single-payer system,” he mentioned in a statement at the time.

Recent findings suggest that mcDermott will also be remembered for some of the attacks he leveled against Republicans. In the most notorious incident, he was ordered to pay then-Rep. John A. Boehner of Ohio — who later became speaker — nearly $1.1 million in 2008 after releasing a recording of a 1996 cell phone call between Boehner and then-Speaker Newt Gingrich. McDermott maintained it was worth the fight, and the cost of the settlement, to protect free speech.

According to recent reports, “Jim McDermott was as massive as it gets in Washington state politics,” Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., wrote on Facebook. “Smart, funny, and Irish, Jim McDermott will be missed.”.

Masked ICE Agents Arrest Father And Daughter Boarding Alaska Airlines Flight, But “Visa Overstay” Is Not The Whole Story

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that ICE arrested a father and daughter as they boarded an Alaska Airlines flight in Seattle, and the government’s explanation is that they overstayed their visas.
  • By now, you may have seen the disturbing passenger recordings from the jet bridge for Alaska Airlines flight 1306 from Seattle to Los Angeles on November 21, 2026.
  • Sources indicate that masked federal officers detained Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and his adult daughter, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, during boarding.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ICE arrested a father and daughter as they boarded an Alaska Airlines flight in Seattle, and the government’s explanation is that they overstayed their visas. But their attorney says they entered legally, have pending immigration applications and valid work permits, and have no criminal history. I support secure borders…but I think this operation deserves a better explanation than “they broke the law.”.

By now, you may have seen the disturbing passenger recordings from the jet bridge for Alaska Airlines flight 1306 from Seattle to Los Angeles on November 21, 2026.

Sources indicate that masked federal officers detained Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and his adult daughter, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, during boarding. The encounter involved a struggle in front of other passengers and delayed the flight.

Recent findings suggest that masked ICE agents detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers were boarding a flight. Alaska Airlines said ICE officers gave them no advance notice of the operation. pic.twitter.com/r44WPTvGdv.

— Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) November 22, 2026.

The crew was so shaken by the incident that replacements had to be called in, delaying the flight for three hours.

Yesterday, the family’s attorney, Olia Catala, claimed they were traveling to California for a family baptism.

According to recent reports, ICE says Mendoza overstayed his visa. It also alleges that Hernandez Mejia threw hot coffee at officers during the encounter and says she could face an assault charge.

On November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.

According to recent reports, during the arrest other travelers began to obstruct and assault our law enforcement officers—a federal crime and a felony. One passenger hurled hot coffee on the officers. Other passengers began obstructing federal officers.

In a recent development, the individual who threw the hot coffee was identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, an illegal alien from Mexico and visa overstay. She was subsequently arrested as well. She will be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

It has been revealed that assaulting and obstructing law enforcement is a crime and a felony. Secretary Mullin has been clear: anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the fullest extent of the law. Our brave law enforcement is facing more than a 1,600% increase in assaults, 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them. This violence must end.

On November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.

During the arrest other travelers began to… https://t.co/nXiBxAqIJ5.

— U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (@ICEgov) November 22, 2026.

The family’s lawyer disputes that account, saying the coffee spilled during the confrontation. An eyewitness has also challenged the government’s description. If Mejia did deliberately throw coffee on officers, she should be held accountable.

The family’s account adds information that is critical to this discussion.

Catala claims the father and daughter entered the United States legally in 2015 and subsequently sought asylum. The father’s application remains pending. The daughter has since married a U.S. citizen and has a separate application to adjust her immigration status. According to their attorney, both have work authorization and neither has a criminal record.

Yes, a work permit is not a Green Card and a pending immigration application does not automatically prevent detention: I am not declaring that ICE lacked legal authority to make these arrests.

Even so, if the government permits someone to work while it considers an immigration application, the expiration of the original tourist admission does not tell us everything we need to know about that person’s circumstances.

We constantly hear that people should come legally and follow the process. Here, the family’s lawyer states they entered legally and have been pursuing that process for years. I’m not seeing any information to justify the raid in hte DHS statement above…I struggle to understand the urgency of arresting these particular travelers on the way to a family baptism.

And sorry, but I don’t think federal agents should be allowed to wear masks. Here it may have violated Washington State law, but it is more fundamental: the masks betray fear…not reasonable fear of crazy people attacking them for doing their jobs…but subconscious fear that they pursuing injustice, not justice, and that there is often a difference between the spirit of the law and the letter of the law.

Industry observers note that I hope that President Trump and the Democratic-controlled Congress can reach a grand bargain on immigration reform. Give Trump his wall if it means a pathway to citizenship for those otherwise law-abiding citizens who may have entered illegally but are now part of the American fabric. Let’s make a deal.

Alaska Airlines published its statement on Saturday afternoon, complaining it was not given notice of the immigration raid:.

“We are concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306. We recognize how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests. Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials. We do not direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity, and we remain committed to protecting the privacy and safety of our guests and employees wherever possible….

“In this instance, Alaska Airlines was not provided appropriate notice of the enforcement action.”.

Recent findings suggest that the airline says it must comply with applicable law, but does not direct or coordinate immigration enforcement. It expressed concern for affected passengers and employees and mentioned it would work with the Port of Seattle and government authorities to determine whether proper protocols were followed.

Alaska too is right to demand answers about an operation that disrupted boarding and left its employees managing the consequences.

The Port of Seattle’s initial statement opened:.

“We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Port stated it did not participate in the enforcement action and was examining with DHS whether previously agreed airport protocols had been breached. On Monday, commissioners went further, calling for a review of airport access and security credentials. Commissioner Sam Cho said:.

Recent findings suggest that “The traveling public and our airport employees should not be left wondering whether they are witnessing a lawful arrest or an abduction. Period”.

That concern strikes me as reasonable. Passengers should be able to identify law enforcement and understand what is happening around them, especially in a confined space immediately outside an aircraft.

Again and again I return to this: whether an agency has authority to act and whether it exercised that authority wisely are separate questions.

I know that interdicting illegal aliens make a lot sense in airports because it is easy to verify where someone is and relatively easy to detain them if you know what flight they will be boarding or arriving on. But on a crowded jetbridge?

A jet bridge is a narrow passageway with passengers carrying bags, sometimes holding children, and often standing in a line that barely moves. There is little room to step away when a confrontation begins.

In a recent development, I see abosutley no need to for these (yes, I see no need for these raids at all for visa overstays without criminal records). I also reject the idea that concern about these tactics means supporting open borders or opposing immigration enforcement. We can enforce immigration laws and still expect the government to exercise restraint and judgment.

For me, the unresolved coffee allegation reinforces the need for a careful review. Deliberately throwing hot coffee at officers would be serious (an accidental spill during a sudden struggle would be a very different matter). The available accounts conflict, and the consequences for the daughter could be substantial.

According to recent reports, there should be an accounting of what occurred before the passenger recordings began, how officers identified themselves, and why this operation unfolded during boarding. I hope more recordings emerge.

It has been revealed that the government claims it arrested visa overstayers. Their lawyer says they have pending immigration applications, work permits, and no criminal history. Both seem to be true, which is precisely why the victory lap by DHS is an inadequate explanation.

Sources indicate that I support enforcing immigration laws, but I want to understand why these travelers were targeted in this manner and whether the force used was justified. The GOP lost massive in the Midterms because reasonable Americans who do support secure borders did not vote for this sort of nefarious tomfoolery. Alaska Airlines and airport officials deserve answers. So do the family and the passengers who found themselves caught in the middle. As I often ask, where are the adults in the room?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that visiting the Galapagos can feel like stepping onto another planet.
  • This unique archipelago of 20 scattered islands—plus dozens more islets and notable rocks in between—is best explored by a specialty cruise.
  • The best Galapagos cruises combine tourism with conservation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that visiting the Galapagos can feel like stepping onto another planet. This chain of volcanic islands is a mystical realm of otherworldly lava formations, sweeping oceanic vistas, ancient flora, and endemic animal species not found anywhere else on earth.

This unique archipelago of 20 scattered islands—plus dozens more islets and notable rocks in between—is best explored by a specialty cruise. Sailing through the Galapagos Islands allows travelers the ease of navigating to the destination’s smaller locales, getting up close to rare wildlife, and the constant presence of naturalists who can maximize every moment, from pointing out passing marine life to guided stargazing on deck.

Ecoventura's Evolve expedition yacht.

The best Galapagos cruises combine tourism with conservation.

The best Galapagos cruises are intimate voyages aboard specialized ships designed to help preserve the islands’ delicate ecosystems. When the day of intrepid exploring is finished, the ship becomes your floating home, offering travelers a serene space to relax and debrief about the wonders you've just experienced. Here’s a look at the best Galapagos cruises to take in 2027, spanning everything from boutique yachts and all-inclusive cruises to top-of-the-line expedition ships.

This article has been updated with newly introduced information since its original publication date.

Ecoventura's Theory is not only luxurious, but it welcomes families (with children ages six and up) with open arms.

For an intimate, curated voyage through the Galapagos, you can’t go wrong with an Ecoventura cruise. The line operates three Relais & Chateaux yachts, Origin, Theory, and Evolve, each of which has just 10 staterooms for a total of 20 guests. Each stateroom offers oversized windows and a sleek, modern design.

Sources indicate that travelers can choose between Ecoventura’s two seven-night itineraries: The “Beaches and Bays” voyage visits San Cristobal, Espanola, Floreana, Santa Cruz, Bartolome, and North Seymour Islands, and the “Volcanic Wonders” sailing calls upon more remote locations like Isabela and Fernandina Islands. (There’s also the option to combine both into a 14-night sailing.).

Industry observers note that the line’s expedition guides, who are trained in birdwatching, stargazing, and nature photography, escort travelers to notable locations, like the red sand beach on Rabida Island with its flocks of American Flamingos, and the iconic pinnacle rock of Bartolome Island. There’s also kayaking, zodiac rides, and snorkeling among sea turtles, sea lions, reef fish, and more. Scuba divers can board the line’s 16-passenger luxury vessel, Galapagos Sky, for multi-day dive excursions to seek out whale sharks, hammerheads, and manta rays.

The ultra-luxe Silver Origin at dusk.

Galápagos sea lions, as seen on a cruise.

One of the most luxurious options in the Galapagos, Silversea has brought its lavish, all-inclusive concept to the rugged archipelago aboard its destination-specific ship Silver Origin. The all-suite, all-balcony vessel holds 100 passengers and offers butler service in every suite, plus an in-room bar stocked to your preferences. Each suite is ultra-spacious, but the villa category offers sweeping terraces, vast living spaces and dining areas, and a separate bedroom. Elsewhere on the ship are two restaurants, a lounge, spa, fitness center, and stargazing platform— collectively, a promise that passengers will never be bored.

Silversea’s seven-day Galapagos itineraries all sail round-trip from the island of San Cristobal. Depending on the exact sailing, voyages call upon a wide variety of islands, including Isabela, Fernandina, North Seymour, Santa Cruz, Espanola, and more. With the included excursions, guests can explore the lunar landscapes of Isabela’s ancient lava flows, witness the seabird sanctuaries of Prince Philip's Steps, participate in guided nature hikes, deep-water snorkeling, zodiac cruises, and kayaking. Luxe touches, like free expedition gear and unlimited pours of Champagne on board, push the voyages over the top. Plus, Silver Origin’s specialized features—like a dynamic positioning system and advanced propulsion—are easier on the local ecosystem's fragile marine life.

The National Geographic Gemini hosts some of the best Galapagos cruises for bringing kids along.

Industry observers note that inspire your kids to learn about science and exploration by hopping on board one of Lindblad Expedition's four Galapagos ships: National Geographic Endeavour II, National Geographic Islander II, National Geographic Gemini, and National Geographic Delfina. These journeys, led by National Geographic experts, give kids the chance to become National Geographic Explorers-In-Training. The exclusive, hands-on program is designed to teach kids about geographical exploration and scientific research. The National Geographic Gemini, which debuted in 2025, can accommodate up to 48 passengers in 27 suites. More than a dozen suites come with private balconies, and one of those balconies is large enough to accommodate a private hot tub. But don’t fret if that suite is already booked; there’s a whirlpool hot tub on the sundeck that’s open to all guests. There’s also a library, well-stocked bar, and meals made with locally sourced ingredients on board.

andBeyond's 124-foot expedition yacht Galapagos Explorer.

Recent findings suggest that with its 124-foot expedition yacht, Galapagos Explorer, andBeyond offers a truly exclusive experience. The yacht has only six rooms to accommodate 12 guests, and it’s also available for a fully private charter. Across the yacht’s four decks are a hot tub, sun deck, swim deck, as well as indoor and outdoor dining rooms and bars. In the five cabins and one larger suite, passengers will find a warm design accented with an oceanic color palette and natural materials like carved wood accents and indigenous textiles—making the ship feel more like a boutique hotel than a cruise. &Beyond’s seven-day itineraries call upon multiple islands either to the east or west, with a mix of popular and more remote locales, like Genovesa, Bartolome, Santa Cruz, Floreana, Espanola, Isabela, and Santa Fe. Snorkeling, kayaking, guided hikes, and island tours are all part of the daily activities with the expedition team, who can personalize each excursion thanks to the small number of guests on board.

The 164-foot superyacht Aqua Mare carries 16 passengers and 16 crew members.

Sources indicate that the 164-foot superyacht Aqua Mare is all about bespoke attention. The small vessel carries 16 passengers, with 16 crew members to look after guests’ every need. Within the ship’s elegant interiors are seven cabins with gleaming woodwork, marble-accented bathrooms, and an owner’s suite with multiple bedrooms and living spaces.

Spanning the rest of the yacht’s four decks are a panoramic sundeck, hot tub, and indoor and outdoor dining rooms, where chef Pedro Miguel Schiaffino serves up Peruvian Nikkei-style cuisine. Expect selections like potato llapingachos, tuna crudo, barbecued plantains, and shrimp ceviche created with ingredients sourced from local farmers, fishermen, and other purveyors. The lower-deck swim platform and beach club is the launch point for kayaks, paddle boards, and snorkeling, or lazy days by the water.

It has been revealed that itineraries cover a wide breadth of islands, from the northern reaches of Genovesa to the southernmost Espanola, and Santa Fe, Santa Cruz, and Santiago in between. Western-focused itineraries arc around the far West side of Isabela Island, which allows for rarefied activities. Guests can hike among the penguin colonies and lava rocks of Punta Moreno, as well as the saltwater Darwin Lake located inside of a volcanic crater at Caleta Tagus.

Sources indicate that ecuadorian-owned, family-run expedition line Quasar operates 8-day and 15-day safari-style itineraries that focus on facilitating meaningful wildlife encounters for the small group of guests on board. With these immersive sailings, you might be swimming with sea turtles one day and cruising on a Zodiac boat amid a pod of dolphins the next. The line’s two yachts are designed for intimate trips, carrying a maximum of 32 guests. The 16-passenger Grace yacht has an especially intriguing history: Grace Kelly, who used it for her honeymoon in 1956, and has since been carefully restored to its original opulent glory. Guests can even stay in the revamped Grace Kelly suite, where the iconic actress spent her two-week honeymoon. Both yachts offer modern amenities like oversized hot tubs, al-fresco bars and lounges, sun decks, and more. Everything from meals to shore excursions to the open bar is included in the cruise fare.

Guests also have onboard access to kayaks, paddle boards, and snorkeling equipment for interacting directly with marine life like reef sharks, sea lions, and marine iguanas whenever the mood strikes. With such a small group, tours are immersive and personalized. Travelers can expect daily Zodiac landings across remote sites on islands like Espanola, Genovesa, Fernandina, Isabela, and Bartolome with expert naturalist guides.

While Flora can fit up to 100 passengers on board, excursions are limited to groups of 12 guests or fewer.

According to recent reports, sailing aboard the purpose-built ship Celebrity Flora strikes a perfect balance between relaxing on a luxurious floating resort and chasing the thrill of an adventurous expedition. The all-suite, all-veranda ship offers each guest a personal suite attendant, menus curated by a Michelin-starred chef, and an all-inclusive policy that covers drinks, meals, shore excursions, and even flights. Travelers can also expect a personal touch from crew, with 100 passengers on board and excursions that are limited to groups of 12 guests or fewer. Tours included memorable experiences like walks through lava tunnels, panga boat rides along rocky shorelines teeming with Galapagos penguins and sea lions, guided hikes to see blue-footed boobies, frigate birds, giant tortoises, rare flora, and ancient cacti.

Opportunities to spot diverse wildlife don’t end once travelers return to the ship. Celebrity Flora is outfitted with Sky Suites featuring the line’s signature Infinite Veranda that brings the extraordinary outdoor surroundings directly into your room. The window transforms into an open-air veranda at the touch of a button, allowing travelers to fully immerse themselves in the wondrous landscapes without even leaving their room. Plus, features like solar panels, reverse-osmosis water filtration, and dynamic positioning are gentle on the islands’ precious resources.

How early should I book a Galapagos cruise?

Recent findings suggest that for the widest selection of vessels and sailing dates, aim to book your cruise four to nine months ahead of your intended sailing. More spontaneous travelers may find last-minute deals booking two to eight weeks ahead of their intended departure, though some itineraries will be sold out by then.

Where do I embark on a Galapagos cruise?

Getting to the Galapagos requires some logistical planning. After flying into Quito or Guayaquil, passengers typically spend a night in one of these mainland destinations before flying to the islands to board their ships. Your cruise line will tell you where to be on the islands for your departure, and in some cases, flights from the mainland will be included (or booked for an additional fee).

When is the best time to cruise the Galapagos Islands?

Industry observers note that with a consistently mild climate year-round, the Galapagos can be visited at any time, although certain seasons offer exceptional wildlife viewing. December is when the giant tortoises hatch, and July marks the mating season for blue-footed boobies and short-eared owls. In April and May, marine iguanas typically hatch, while sea turtles begin laying their eggs at the start of the year. Given the diverse wildlife and year-round natural phenomena, there's never a "wrong" time to visit the islands.

Are Galapagos cruises expensive?

In a recent development, the Galapagos Islands aren’t a bargain destination. Expect to pay somewhere between $5,000 and $12,000 per traveler, depending on the ship, itinerary, and length of the voyage, though there are options starting in the $3,000s.

What kind of wildlife can I expect to see on a Galapagos cruise?

The Galapagos Islands are renowned for their unique wildlife, including giant tortoises, marine iguanas, blue-footed boobies, and sea lions. The islands’ ecosystems are so diverse that you can see a variety of species in different environments, from volcanic shores to lush highlands.

American Airlines Expands Block On Last-Minute Partner Award Bookings

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (801 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, american Airlines appears to have expanded a frustrating restriction on last-minute award travel.
  • Industry observers note that as first flagged by One Mile At A Time, American is now withholding saver award inventory on wholly domestic connecting itineraries within 144 hours of departure.
  • Recent findings suggest that american began blocking domestic nonstop saver awards within that window in May.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, american Airlines appears to have expanded a frustrating restriction on last-minute award travel. Domestic connections are now subject to the same six-day cutoff that already blocked nonstop saver awards through partner programs. For travelers using Alaska Atmos Rewards points or British Airways Avios, another useful way to book American flights seems to have vanished.

Industry observers note that as first flagged by One Mile At A Time, American is now withholding saver award inventory on wholly domestic connecting itineraries within 144 hours of departure. The restriction affects both economy and premium cabins.

Recent findings suggest that american began blocking domestic nonstop saver awards within that window in May. Connections initially remained available, but that appears to have changed. International itineraries, including those with domestic connections, reportedly remain outside this restriction.

Recent findings suggest that when using AA miles, there appears to be no change. AAdvantage members can still book flights through American itself, where award prices vary. The restriction concerns the inventory that other frequent flyer programs need to sell an award on American.

First, a short primer…each day this blog has folks who have read it for almost 20 years and those who are reading it for the first time.

A seat available for miles on AA.com is not necessarily available to Alaska or British Airways. American controls what it releases to those programs, and its own award pricing varies by flight and date.

When the original restriction emerged, flights disappeared from partner searches as they crossed the six-day threshold, even while remaining available through AAdvantage.

Sources indicate that so an empty search result on a partner website does not necessarily mean the flight is full or that American has stopped accepting miles. It may simply mean you have the wrong kind of miles….

Industry observers note that I understand why American might prefer that someone book through AAdvantage rather than redeem another airline’s currency. Giving travelers a reason to accumulate its own miles has commercial value and is part of AA’s blueprint to return to profitability.

But understanding the incentive does not make this a welcome development.

One of the most useful things about miles is being able to arrange a trip when cash fares are high. Think family emergency or holiday travel.

In those circumstances, having access to American through another program can be very valuable. Removing that option makes the points already sitting in those accounts less useful, even if the published award chart does not change.

Industry observers note that we spend plenty of time discussing award price increases, but availability deserves just as much attention. An attractive mileage price is of little practical value when the program cannot book the flight you need, which is frequent criticism of Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards, now even less valuable than due to AA blocking space.

No one is asking American to release every unsold seat to every partner….AA has every right to monetize as many seats as it can, just like it doing with first class upgrades.

Still, I would rather see American manage availability flight by flight than impose a broad cutoff based on how soon someone wants to travel. A flight with weak demand and a flight that is nearly sold out do not present the same commercial circumstances.

American does not comment on program changes like this, but has apparently concluded that the additional control is worth the lost partner bookings. Without knowing the reimbursement arrangements, I am not going to pretend I can calculate that trade-off.

From the passenger perspective, however, this is another reason to temper expectations about airline partnerships. The ability to earn points in one program and redeem them across a network is a major selling point. Restrictions like this make that promise less useful…and this is hardly a unique trend: we see the same thing with Delta and United.

If you need an American flight within six days of departure, check AAdvantage directly, for now that is your only option. Always compare the mileage price with the cash fare too…using miles is not automatically the better deal and is often not.

It has been revealed that for travel farther out, I would still compare partner options before booking. But I would be certainly not transfer points speculatively while hoping that domestic American availability will open shortly before departure.

Recent findings suggest that the expansion of partner award blocking removes another option for travelers hoping to use miles for last-minute domestic American flights. AAdvantage remains an option, but it’s a big blow to Alaska Airlines Atmos members.

I understand why American wants to favor its own program. Even so, I cannot celebrate this news.
