  • Senate Republicans appeared skeptical Monday about the need for as much as $50 billion to upgrade the nation’s aging air traffic control system, after a nationwide ground stop last Friday prompted the massive, increased asking price from top administration officials.
  • Speaking with reporters, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said he believed the department still had about $8 billion outstanding from an air traffic control modernization package included in last year’s reconciliation law.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., speaks with reporters on Nov. 10. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Republicans appeared skeptical Monday about the need for as much as $50 billion to upgrade the nation’s aging air traffic control system, after a nationwide ground stop last Friday prompted the massive, increased asking price from top administration officials.

Speaking with reporters, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said he believed the department still had about $8 billion outstanding from an air traffic control modernization package included in last year’s reconciliation law.

“I got to obviously see the explanation behind it, or sort of laying out the numbers why it's necessary,” Thune said of the $50 billion, which jumped from $30 billion a day earlier.

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., told reporters he was unimpressed by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s request and that he wanted to see a breakdown of how the department would use the funds.

According to recent reports, “They got to give us an update,” Tillis said. “I mean, the $50 billion request — I thought that was $30 billion. So people have got to explain to me, really, even the basis for the $30 billion, let alone the additional $20 billion that Duffy mentioned the other day.”.

Industry observers note that sen. John Hoeven, R-N.D., similarly remarked legislators would need “more detail” on the request but said “obviously there needs to be more” funding for the modernization efforts.

Hoeven serves on the Senate Transportation-HUD Appropriations Subcommittee, which rolled out a fiscal 2027 spending bill Monday that would increase the FAA’s annual allocation to facilities and equipment by $500 million, a nearly 13 percent boost.

It has been revealed that duffy is slotted to attend the Senate GOP conference lunch on Tuesday, where he is likely to be peppered with such requests for specifics. Meanwhile, FAA staff are expected to brief House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee aides on Tuesday, after that meeting got pushed on Monday.

The Senate’s go-slow approach is in contrast to Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., who stated over the weekend that he would add the $50 billion request to a year-end legislative package.

The White House’s call for additional funds ballooned last week in the aftermath of the nationwide ground stop that created confusion and concern at airports around the country. The Federal Aviation Administration remarked Sunday that the unusual move was made “out of an abundance of caution” after legacy equipment became flooded with data during routine upgrades.

The FAA’s initial investigation tied the data flooding to work being done at a radar site in Texas and a radio communications site in Arkansas by contractor L3Harris Technologies.

Speaking on CNBC’s Squawk Box, Duffy mentioned the server thought to have caused the flooding was taken to the L3Harris lab in Florida where FAA personnel are working with the FBI to analyze the router that likely caused the system instability.

Still, as administration officials attempt to understand the system errors that led to the ground stop, Duffy has used the moment as justification to lobby for additional funds.

According to recent reports, “In this old telecom network, I do have money to switch over from the old copper wires to fiber and we’re 70 percent completed with that mission, but we need a brand latest architecture for our telecom and aviation,” Duffy mentioned on CNBC Monday. “This can happen quickly to build a new state of the art telecom network, it’s just that it has to be funded.”.

Industry observers note that A day before the incident, Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought wrote to congressional appropriators, formally asking for $30.1 billion in added funds for the modernization effort, in line with a bill introduced by Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., in late September. That ask inexplicably jumped up to $50 billion by Friday night in the aftermath of the ground stop.

On Monday, Thune noted the prior request for approximately $30 billion, which he said included “some other stuff” as well.

Schmitt’s bill and the White House request would provide $10.1 billion for air traffic control upgrades, including $7.2 billion for a “common automation platform and a common controller workstation,” and $2 billion for cloud computing and telecommunications infrastructure.

Another $10 billion would go toward airport improvement projects, including $2 billion to “construct, replace, and improve terminal air traffic control facilities, including activities using digital tower technologies.”.

The request includes $10 billion for a terminal modernization or reconstruction pilot program for certain midsized airports.

Thune said Monday that he tallied about $12 billion in the new request specifically for air traffic control related issues, likely a reference to the $10.1 billion plus the $2 billion for terminal facilities.

In a recent development, “I think there's more we need to figure out, and obviously I think we all agree that we need to be modernizing and updating, particularly in an area like that where safety is the number one priority, but also we want to do that in a smart way and make sure that we're using taxpayer dollars wisely and well,” Thune said. “We’ll hear him out.”.

Meanwhile, Democrats kept up the drumbeat of criticism, both for the airspace management that led to the ground stop and the rollout of the fresh funding request.

According to recent reports, “So typical of this incompetent administration — they have money, they don’t use it and then they come back and say ‘give us more money,'” Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., said on the floor.

Savannah Behrmann and Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

Breaking: This Cruise Proves the Congo is No Heart of Darkness—Or Viral Fad

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1317 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that occasionally, a place will take hold of our collective imagination in much the same way that an unsolved mathematical problem does, or a treasure hunt, or an ancient, coded message found moldering in an attic, beguiling with its mystery, difficulty, and promise of a reward.
  • It has been revealed that the idea could be remarked to originate in the late 19th century, as Europeans made their way into the great forests seeking fortune and glory.
  • Dzanga Baï, a protected area in the southwestern Central African Republic also known as “the village of elephants.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that occasionally, a place will take hold of our collective imagination in much the same way that an unsolved mathematical problem does, or a treasure hunt, or an ancient, coded message found moldering in an attic, beguiling with its mystery, difficulty, and promise of a reward. Few places exert quite this pull like the Congo Basin, a thick block of forest and rivers covering much of Central Africa, home to some 150 ethnic groups, and a raft of extraordinary biodiversity. Despite its size and its importance as a counterbalance to climate change, the region endures a dearth of scientific research funding and conservation efforts. Roughly the size of India, it has inspired and vexed many visitors (even those who might otherwise have claimed to have conquered it).

A floating village in the Congo River Basin.

It has been revealed that the idea could be remarked to originate in the late 19th century, as Europeans made their way into the great forests seeking fortune and glory. The Welsh explorer Henry Morton Stanley, the first to leave a detailed record of his journey across the Basin, claimed that even after a three-year trek (1874-77) it remained “a region of fable and mystery.” That was exactly the mix sought by Polish sailor Józef Korzeniowski, who, as a boy, looked at the map of Africa, then a white space, and “declared that some day I would go there.” Eventually, and not long after Stanley, he did, and with the captaincy of a steamboat on the Congo River, was tasked with collecting one Mr. Klein, an upcountry agent employed by the brutal Belgian trading company. Korzeniowski was horrified by what he saw along the river—colonization and resource extraction at its cruelest and bloodiest—calling it “the vilest scramble for loot that ever disfigured the history of human conscience and geographical exploration.” Later, Józef Korzeniowski became Joseph Conrad, Mr. Klein became Mr. Kurtz, and the rest is literary history.

Dzanga Baï, a protected area in the southwestern Central African Republic also known as “the village of elephants.”.

The latest journeyman to apply themself to the region is another Welshman, Ash Dykes, whose TikTok videos of his journey paddling down the Sangha River (a tributary of the mighty Congo River) have received millions of views. By mid-October, Dykes, who calls himself an extreme athlete, was midway through the 400 miles he hoped to cover. His videos—the anxiety and speculation of his preparation; the amplification of the danger en route—are over-exaggerated, designed to amuse his audience; they are spectacle. Looking bewildered in his state-of-the-art inflatable boat, Dykes is most often met by competent, unaffected locals, paddling their wooden pirogues with balletic grace. And brave though Dykes certainly is, most of what he has accomplished—attending a hunt with the Ba’aka people, seeing the forest elephants in Dzanga Baï, or tracking Western lowland gorillas—can be done by just about anyone.

The Princesse Ngalessa, a multi-level riverboat operated by Ducret Expeditions, is the basin's only passenger cruise.

I, too, was one enchanted by the inscrutability of the Congo Basin, and I dreamt of one day traveling along its rivers and into its forests; in my mind’s eye, I envisioned dusk slipping into night, to the rhythm of a pounding drumbeat. Not long ago, I departed Brazzaville, the capital of the Republic of Congo, aboard the Princesse Ngalessa, a multi-level riverboat operated by Ducret Expeditions. As the only such passenger vessel in the Congo Basin, the crew of the Ngalessa is accustomed to receiving rarefied looks from the riverbank. But just as often, the ship’s approach was greeted with aplomb, for it was an event in the villages and brought goods, along with community support and news from away.

Industry observers note that in comparison to the coarse and crowded daka-dakas—flat-topped river barges, stuffed with goods and spewing black, acrid smoke as they chunter between Kinshasa and Kisangani—those of us onboard the Ngalessa traveled in glorious comfort: air-conditioning, three square meals a day, and private bathrooms. We also had the benefit of our local guides and their familiarity with the languages, customs, and faces up and down the river. This included, in the riverside village of Ngabe, the appearance of an Ejengi, a forest spirit made of palm fronds that danced and spun as a crowd of onlookers sang, drummed, and screamed in delight.

According to recent reports, “Don’t worry,” our guide said. “Look at his dusty bare feet!” Elsewhere, we watched an Indigenous Luma woman cut, strip, and chew twigs into a pulp that could be used as medicinal pain relief. On other days, we kayaked through the flooded forests of the Alima River, and traded with fishermen who brought their slim pirogues against our mammoth ship to hand over smoked fish and fruit.

Kayaking through the flooded forests of the Alima River.

Eight days and 600 miles after leaving Brazzaville, we arrived at the outpost of Ouesso on the Sangha River. I journeyed further upon that water by launch boat, into the Central African Republic, and spent days at Sangha Lodge, drinking gin and tonics with local legend Rod Cassidy, an eco-tourism pioneer who has spent years living and working with the local Ba’aka people. It was through him I had the good luck to attend a hunt with those same Ba’aka, and to look on while they divvied up the duiker they snagged in their homemade nets. Afterwards, they whooped and hollered as they carried the meat out and into their village—a feast!

Recent findings suggest that in the heightened state of travel, there comes occasionally a moment like falling into an empty space and, as two glancing stones can spark a blaze, a light of comprehension is illuminated. Sometimes this moment manifests itself as love, other times as admiration, or confusion. Conrad left the Congo in spiritual, psychological, and physical shock. “Before the Congo, I was a mere animal,” he wrote after his consequential journey. He was changed, as travelers who go forward with their ears and eyes open (to say nothing of their hearts) are changed. Watching the Ba’aka poised in their hunt, ears tilted to the slightest sound, I felt myself see humanity as it had existed since time immemorial. As they laughed and chatted on their success, the women showing their fangs (chipped with rocks as a show of strength), and the men slapping each other on the back, I could barely remember seeing such happiness elsewhere.

According to recent reports, the Congo Basin may still be raw and atavistic—great adventures there are still possible—but it is no “heart of darkness” (a title which for Conrad lay not in the location itself, but rather mankind’s ability to exploit and vilify others). What separates it from other places is its independence. It requires protection, yes, but has no need, and few provisions, for any prying visitors; it is not a prize to be conquered. Most incredibly, it remains the home of peoples who have not yet latched themselves to tourism; people who sustain themselves almost wholly from an expanse of forest and the waters that for others can only be the basis of wonder and amazement. And yet, after all the sorrow and misery that colonialism brought to the Congo Basin, the people remain sincere and earnest, and willing to show others the best of their land.

A lone kayaker glides underneath a hazy sky.

One night, as the Ngalessa drifted northward, from beneath the awning on the ship’s upper deck, I watched a cloud bank clump and darken. Finally, with an incision of lightning, the downpour came, brief but fierce. The sun returned, low in the sky but still warm, and the scent of damp earth rose up. A patter of drumming reached us from somewhere, before being swallowed by the forest. The dinner bell rang, and I thought I never want this trip to end.

#111389. No more permanent coalitions: What the midterm results reveal

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (919 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

No more permanent coalitions: What the midterm results reveal

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (919 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that senate Democratic leader Charles E.
  • ANALYSIS -- “Life moves pretty fast,” that famed 20th-century philosopher Ferris Bueller once mentioned.
  • In 2024, Democrats were consigned to the political wilderness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer poses in his office on Nov. 9 for a group photo with incoming members of his caucus: from left, Ohio's Sherrod Brown, Texas' James Talarico, Iowa's Josh Turek, Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed, North Carolina's Roy Cooper, Illinois' Juliana Stratton, Fresh Hampshire's Chris Pappas, South Carolina's Annie Andrews, Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan, Maine's Troy Jackson and Kansas' Adam Hamilton. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

ANALYSIS -- “Life moves pretty fast,” that famed 20th-century philosopher Ferris Bueller once mentioned. “If you don't stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.”.

In 2024, Democrats were consigned to the political wilderness. Republicans had captured the White House, flipped the Senate and held the House. President Donald Trump had completely altered the party coalitions as he led the ascendant GOP to victory.

Recent findings suggest that now, just two years later, Democrats are on the rise. A historic midterm tsunami has swept them into such commanding Senate and House majorities that some are questioning whether Republicans will ever be in charge again. And if Texas is blue, how does the GOP have any chance in the Electoral College again?

A big takeaway from the midterm results should be that there’s very little permanence in our politics.

What may have looked like a newly introduced GOP coalition was really more of a Trump coalition, and it crumbled in the face of economic frustrations, affordability concerns and the president’s unpopular policies.

With Trump’s negative job approval rating weighing them down, Republican candidates suffered losses among virtually all demographic groups – including by wide margins among constituencies thought to make up the GOP’s core.

Trump or the Republicans finished ahead among male voters by 4 points in 2018, 8 points in 2020, 14 points in 2022 and 12 points in 2024, according to the exit polls. Men went for Democratic candidates by 4 points (51 percent to 47 percent) this cycle. Meanwhile, Republicans lost even more ground among women. While Kamala Harris finished ahead of Trump by 8 points in 2024, that margin grew to 21 points for Democratic candidates this year.

Recent findings suggest that trump closed the gap among Hispanic voters to just 5 points behind Harris two years ago. This year, Hispanic voters nationwide supported Democratic candidates by 32 points (65 percent to 33 percent). Even white voters shifted significantly. They backed Trump or  Republican candidates by 10 points in 2018, 17 points in 2020, 18 points in 2022 and 15 points in 2024. And yet Democrats edged out Republicans by a point (50 percent to 49 percent) on Nov. 3.

Voters without a college degree were supposed to be a key cog in Republicans’ fresh populist coalition. But they went from +13 (56 percent to 43 percent) for Trump in 2024 to backing Republican candidates by just 1 point this year. Meanwhile, the gap among voters with a college degree went from 14 points for Harris in 2024 to 30 points for Democrats this cycle.

Industry observers note that republicans had closed the gap among young voters aged 18 to 29 from 35 points in 2018 to just 11 points in 2024. But younger voters supported Democratic candidates this year by 50 points (74 percent to 24 percent). Not to mention Democrats flipped voters aged 45 to 64 for the first time in nearly two decades.

In a recent development, white evangelicals appear to be one of the only groups that didn’t shift toward Democrats. They supported GOP candidates 82 percent to 17 percent. But they only made up 17 percent of the electorate, according to the exit polls, which is down from a very consistent 25 percent for more than a decade. So there was still a problem with that group of voters, but it was more about turnout than persuasion.

Sources indicate that while there was an unmistakable leftward shift this year, the results should not be considered a permanent party realignment any more than 2024 was. While Democrats did extremely well in Texas this year, they still haven’t won the Lone Star State in a presidential race in 50 years. So maybe it’s wise for everyone to take a deep breath.

Industry observers note that if you take this year’s election results and match them with the Senate seats on the ballot in 2028, there doesn’t appear to be a viable path for Republicans back to the majority. But there wasn’t a particularly viable Democratic path to the Senate majority at this point two years ago. And if the Alaska election goes their way, they will end up winning Senate races in seven states that were initially rated Solid Republican.

Industry observers note that if one party starts to get too comfortable, voters have a way of bringing politicians back down to earth. If Democrats come to Congress and push too far to the left or become too defined by their most extreme members, they will squander the opportunity they earned this year.

The dramatic demographic swings should be evidence that many voters are not beholden to either party and are open to switching allegiances, particularly in a time of economic uncertainty.

Industry observers note that at the same time, if Republicans don’t go through some time of reflection and instead triple down on the policies that led to the blue wave, they risk cementing some of the shifts that started this cycle. It just won’t be thick cement.

#111388. The 11 Most Beautiful Beaches in the Caribbean

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1101 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

The 11 Most Beautiful Beaches in the Caribbean

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1101 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, picking the most beautiful beaches in the Caribbean is an exercise in splitting hairs.
  • Barbuda is the quieter, more elusive sister to Antigua, but Princess Diana Beach is the reason many visitors make a detour here.
  • Sources indicate that grace Bay is famous for good reason: roughly three miles of powdery white sand and shockingly clear waters make even the most airbrushed postcards look inadequate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, picking the most beautiful beaches in the Caribbean is an exercise in splitting hairs. Nearly every island has a stretch of powdery sand and improbably blue water, and after a while, the “nice sand, nice water” trope stops registering at all. We’re talking beauty in the transcendental sense—the kind of beauty that makes you feel something. Maybe it’s a crescent of sand more pink than you thought could happen in nature. Maybe it’s a labyrinth of granite boulders spilling into the sea. Or maybe it’s a beach bar so perfectly placed it feels as much a part of the landscape as the sand. Plenty of beaches are picturesque. These are the ones, if you ask us, that are beautiful.

Barbuda is the quieter, more elusive sister to Antigua, but Princess Diana Beach is the reason many visitors make a detour here. The long stretch of blush-pink sand is framed by low vegetation and blissfully few signs of life. There is, almost puzzlingly, a Nobu, which brings a welcome blip of civilization in the form of Japanese-Peruvian cooking, cocktails, and a beach club with cabanas. (Nobu Beach Inn is set to debut in 2027, too.) Book lunch there and a beach transfer in advance—many of the top resorts on Antigua offer this as a day excursion from the other island.

Sources indicate that grace Bay is famous for good reason: roughly three miles of powdery white sand and shockingly clear waters make even the most airbrushed postcards look inadequate. An offshore reef keeps the waters agreeably calm for swimming (especially with kids), too. This is one of the Caribbean’s most polished beach destinations, with a concentration of luxury resorts, watersports operators and restaurants that make a choose-your-own adventure beach day a pretty seamless affair. Public access points are plentiful and free, so you needn’t be staying at one of the grand hotels to enjoy the view. (Although you should.).

The kind of place that castaway dreams are made of, Little Bay is a tiny crescent of sand tucked beneath towering limestone cliffs. No beach club, no cabanas, no infrastructure, no fuss. It’s accessible by boat from neighboring Crocus Bay, or, if you’re feeling adventurous, by rope down the rock face. Bring water, a picnic and all your gear—there’s fantastic snorkeling here.

A mile-long horseshoe of white sand with clear, shallow water, Flamenco Beach is more than worth the ferry over from mainland Puerto Rico. It also has an unusual bit of history: two abandoned United States military tanks, left behind after the Navy used Culebra for training exercises, now sit near the shore, covered in colorful graffiti. We aren’t usually proponents of littering, but the counterpoint of natural beauty with human history is part of what makes this beach so unforgettable.

According to recent reports, definitely the most photographed beach in the U.S. Virgin Islands and probably the most photographed beach in the Caribbean, Trunk Bay never disappoints. From the access road, you see a sweep of white sand stretching out, with impossibly turquoise waters and a small offshore cay that seems placed for composition. It’s part of Virgin Islands National Park, so the infrastructure covers all the stuff you need—snack bar, restrooms, showers and snorkel rentals. The main attraction is the underwater snorkeling trail, where submerged markers introduce visitors to the coral reef and its inhabitants.

If you want swanky French beach clubs, head over to Saint-Jean, because Saline is St. Barth’s at its most elemental. The sand is broad and soft, the dunes rolling, and the sea open, with no beach clubs or hotels or influencers interrupting your view. Getting there requires a short walk over the dunes from the parking lot, which helps preserve the feeling that you’re leaving the chi-chi side of the island behind.

It has been revealed that there are beautiful beaches, and then there are the Baths, a landscape so distinctive it feels like you’ve left the Caribbean, and perhaps earth entirely. The beach is home to a collection of enormous granite boulders, some as large as houses, all tumbled together to create something totally unique. Between them are hidden grottoes, tidal pools and narrow passages—making this as much a playground as it is a beach. Bring sturdy water shoes and expect to do some scrambling.

Industry observers note that the longest beach on its island, this elegant crescent sits directly on the Tropic of Cancer. It’s relatively remote and unspoiled by Bahamian standards, making it a true bucket list destination for beach snobs. It’s about a 30-minute drive from George Town on Great Exuma (where the airport is), across the bridge to Little Exuma. There are no proper facilities, so pack what you need. There are Aman, Rosewood and Bulgari resorts debuting here in the years to come—so visit now for serious “I've been coming here since” bragging rights.

Recent findings suggest that A hidden gem by any standard, Sandy Island is a miniature, uninhabited coral cay located just off the west coast of Carriacou, Grenada’s sister island. There are no hotels or roads, and the whole appeal is the rugged simplicity of arriving by boat, dropping anchor and spending an afternoon doing basically nothing except enjoying the elements. The island is part of a protected marine park, making it a fantastic spot for snorkeling with colorful reef fish, turtles and octopi.

Recent findings suggest that the rest of the world is finally catching up with what the diving scene has known for years—No Name Beach is one of the most pristine, stunning stretches of sand anywhere in the Caribbean. It’s located on the tiny island of Klein Bonaire (“Little Bonaire”) just offshore of mainland Bonaire, and is part of Bonaire National Marine Park, meaning development is off the table. There aren’t any restaurants, bathrooms, or beach bars, but there are water taxis from Kralendijk. Bring food and water, your own snorkel gear, and prepare to be blown away by the untouched Caribbean at its finest.

While Bávaro Beach proper is about 5 miles long, it connects seamlessly with adjoining beaches Arena Blanca and Arena Gorda—so, depending on who’s counting, actually comes in at closer to 30 miles of uninterrupted shoreline. This is the beach that initially spurred Punta Cana’s resort boom, with coconut palms fringing the white sand, a barrier reef keeping the waters tranquil, and enough space for everyone to stretch out and (pretty much) never feel crowded. If you head toward El Cortecito or Los Corales, you’ll find beach bars where the party never stops. On a beach this beautiful, why would it?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that when Norse Atlantic Airways commenced operations four years ago, in June 2022, a new dawn for transatlantic travel appeared to have arrived. The carrier promised low-cost long-haul flights using a modern fleet of Boeing 787 Dreamliners, operating from Oslo Gardermoen Airport (OSL) in Norway and, via its UK division, Gatwick Airport (LGW) in London. Now, however, the airline is on the brink.

    This morning, Norse issued a statement about its financial situation and the strategic review it is undertaking as it looks to return to more stable economic ground. The carrier described its financial footing as 'critical' and underlined the need to secure financing to remain operationally viable.

    Norse did not mince its words in Wednesday's statement, explaining outright that "the company’s financial situation is critical" and "dependent on securing financing to meet its short-term liquidity needs and to continue its operations." Given the carrier's well-documented financial struggles, Norse is exploring various options for its future.

    It has been revealed that in this regard, the airline explained on Wednesday morning that it continues to "entertain discussions for a potential takeover." Elsewhere, other options include placing greater emphasis on ACMI (wet lease) contractsto make up for its financial shortfall. The news will concern the airline's flyers and staff, and it has committed to "providing further information as and when appropriate." The airline also remarked it is in "discussions" with agencies to help with its finances.

    "Norse is also engaged in discussions with selected parties on short-term financing. However, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution.".

    In a recent development, when Norse commenced operations back in June 2022, its first route linked Oslo with John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) in Newly introduced York City. Certain flights on this route operated via London, giving passengers flying between the UK and Norway the rare chance to fly short-haul on a 787. Norse then set up a UK subsidiary, allowing it to serve London without the Norway leg.

    Today, Asian leisure destinations also play an vital role in Norse's winter network. According to Cirium, an aviation analytics organization, Norse itself is operating scheduled flights from Oslo and Stockholm to Bangkok and Phuket in Thailand this month. Norse UK is operating flights from London Gatwick to Bangkok and Cape Town, with Orlando being its only US destination.

    According to recent reports, fleet-wise, data from ch-aviation shows that Norse currently has a total of 12 787-9s. Of these, seven are registered in Norway, and five are registered in the UK. Interestingly, three of Norse Atlantic's five UK-registered Boeing 787s are already being used on ACMI contracts, with Pakistan International Airlines listed as their wet-lease customer.

    Sources indicate that the fact that Norse has described its financial situation as critical casts serious doubt on the long-term economic viability of its operations. Unfortunately, the low-cost long-haul market is a difficult nut to crack, as has been proven time and again over the years. Another notable example of a failure on this front involved Norwegian Air Shuttle and its 787s.

    According to recent reports, these Dreamliners operated low-cost intercontinental flights using both Boeing 787-8s (Norwegian Long Haul) and 787-9s (Norwegian Long-Haul and Norwegian Air UK). Much like Norse Atlantic, the carrier promised big things when it came to revolutionizing the long-haul scene for budget-conscious flyers. Unfortunately, the onset of the coronavirus pandemic brought these plans screeching to a sudden halt.

    Beginner’s luck: Freshmen leave it to chance at House office lottery

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (907 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress.
    • As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.
    • Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.

    Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.

    “This is so nervewracking,” she mentioned, before pulling out a chip with a “1” printed on it.

    Her prize was a coveted one — first choice of office space. Every two years, incoming members of the House play a game of chance to see who can land the best real estate and who will be relegated to less desirable corners of the Capitol complex.

    The room broke out in raucous applause and a standing ovation. Her fresh colleagues started singing “Happy Birthday.”.

    Not everyone was so lucky. Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira, R-Texas, pulled number 105 — the very last one. The former MLB player raised his arms in a mock celebration.

    “Lets all hope for the luck of the Taylors,” said Rep.-elect Brent Taylor, R-Tenn., only to emerge with number 81.

    The newly-elected members got their turn in a random order, walking up one by one to a table where deputy executive director of House Office Buildings Kornell Rancy kept watch over the box of chips.

    Sources indicate that rep.-elect John Cowan, R-Ga., was the first to pick a number. The first neurosurgeon to be elected to Congress, Cowan wore his white doctor’s coat as he pulled number 11 out of the box.

    “I wanted to do something where I’m just representing health care providers around the country,” Cowan noted.

    As returning members lay claim to more desirable offices made available by those who resign, retire or lose elections, the space they’ve abandoned is left for the newcomers, who are on the Hill this week for orientation. Many of them will end up in the Longworth Building, where suites can be awkward or cramped.

    Industry observers note that not all offices are created equal, and the calculus has changed over the years. The previously undesirable Cannon Building just underwent a budget-busting renovation that lasted more than a decade, with a spacious courtyard opening earlier this year. But the coveted Rayburn Building still retains its prestige, despite repeated and dire warnings from the Architect of the Capitol about its crumbling infrastructure.

    “You’re welcome,” said Rep.-elect Amish Shah, D-Ariz., after pulling a disappointing number 94.

    Prior to the lottery, Rep.-elect Trever Nehls, R-Texas, was hoping for the best but had a backup blueprint in case his number said otherwise.

    It has been revealed that “If I don’t pick number one, I’m going to offer one of these cigars as a trade to whoever gets it,” he noted, pointing to three of them sticking out of his jacket pocket. He’s preparing to take over the seat currently held by his twin brother Troy, who shares a fondness for stogies.

    In a recent development, the office space lottery dates back to 1908, when members of the 60th Congress received their first office assignments after the completion of what would be named the Cannon Building. A House page drew names and numbers from a box, and members selected their offices from a chart, according to House Office Buildings executive director of facility operations Joe Yates, who kicked things off Tuesday with a history lesson.

    The lottery now is a little more modern, with members poring over virtual office layouts and doing walkthroughs of spaces on laptops.

    “If somebody had to get 105, I’m glad it was me because I am here to serve, and I’m serving my freshman class by picking the worst office,” Teixeira stated. “This is low on my priority list.”.

    Some members announced their lucky draws themselves, while others let Yates break the news.

    “Come visit me,” mentioned Rep.-elect Chris Gober, R-Texas, after pulling number 2 from the box.

    After the lottery itself, members huddled with their staff to strategize about the next steps — how to leverage their numbers and select the best suites left on the list, while also exploring layouts, paint colors and carpeting.

    “First and foremost, a good layout, so we can do good work, and people can be comfortable in doing the work, and then a convenient location. Very utilitarian,” said Rep.-elect Scott Wiener, D-Calif., of his priorities.

    “We’ll get a decent Longworth office,” stated Wiener, who drew pick 43. “Cannon would have been ideal, but I’m happy with any office.”.

    It has been revealed that rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, D-Colo., was hoping to replicate the good luck of some of his colleagues. “I’m going to do the Shannon Taylor and Sam Forstag. It’s eyes closed, behind the back,” he mentioned of his moves, reaching into the box. But it wasn’t enough, and Rutinel pulled number 69.

    “These are not red numbers, these are not blue numbers. These are the remaining numbers, and there ain’t that many,” noted Rep.-elect Johnny Garcia, D-Texas, who was among the last few people to pick. He emerged with number 75.

    And when Rep.-elect Joe Strada, R-Fla., the last of the incoming members to draw, walked up to the table, the whole room cheered.

    “Wouldn’t it be crazy if I picked number 1?” he joked, pulling out the last chip in the box.

    Industry News: I Flew A United Airlines Boeing 737 MAX From A Remote Island Airport With Just 2 Weekly Flights: Here's What It Was Like

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • From its regional hub in Guam, United Airlines is the only airline that provides regular air connections to some of the small Micronesian islands in the Pacific.
    • According to recent reports, one of the most notable regional flight connections United offers is the famous Island Hopper, which flies from Guam to Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae, Kwajalein, Majuro, and Honolulu, and back again.
    • Describing island hopping in Micronesia with United is often much more about the experience at the airport than with United itself.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    From its regional hub in Guam, United Airlines is the only airline that provides regular air connections to some of the small Micronesian islands in the Pacific. Flying on some of these routes is a memorable experience, with local airports operating a TSA- and FAA-compliant system on sleepy little islands. Some island airports only wake up for a flight every second day. In November 2026, I flew from the island of Yap (a state in the Federated States of Micronesia or FSM) to Guam on board a United flight.

    According to recent reports, one of the most notable regional flight connections United offers is the famous Island Hopper, which flies from Guam to Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae, Kwajalein, Majuro, and Honolulu, and back again. I wanted to take this flight to Majuro, but it was beyond my budget. Some United Micronesia flights operate only twice a week, meaning the flight schedule dictates the tour schedule. On the upside, many of these Micronesian flights routinely operate half-full, meaning booking out is unusual for certain routes.

    Describing island hopping in Micronesia with United is often much more about the experience at the airport than with United itself. Yap International Airport is served only by United flights (with 737s) twice a week from Guam and by Pacific Missionary Aviation's (PMA) Beechcraft Super King Air 200 flights (with seven to nine passengers) once a week from Palau. PMA is set to introduce a second weekly flight next year.

    According to recent reports, as these are Yap's only regularly scheduled passenger flights, the airport is generally otherwise closed. I flew from Palau to Yap with PMA and then to Guam with United Airlines. As explained below, PMA offers the only scheduled passenger access to Yap for those who cannot pass through US immigration.

    According to recent reports, there are no direct flights connecting the State of Yap with the three other far-flung states of Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae​​​​​. To access those other islands and avoid United (and US immigration), the main alternative is Nauru Airlines. United's flight from Yap to Guam departs at 2:30 am, arriving in Guam at around 4:00 am, making it difficult to decide whether to book a hotel for the night before, the night of, or not at all. I opted not to book.

    Sources indicate that the experience of checking into United's various island flights differs significantly by island and airport. Some airports (especially on Saipan) are much larger and more sophisticated than Yap, but Yap was the one I flew through, and so I will describe that one here. Yap's check-in and baggage drop-off facilities are located in a covered area outside the building. During the check-in process, there is no air conditioning.

    According to recent reports, at the baggage drop-off (positioned before check-in), the staff informed me that their equipment was broken, so my bag would be manually searched. Many of the bags being checked in for the flight were wares in basic boxes and containers by locals to sell on other islands. Check-in was straightforward, with me presenting my current passport and my expired passport with the US visa.

    One of the notable features of Yap is that the country does not collect the exit fee in the airfare. There is a window where passengers must pay the $20 exit fee before going to the adjacent immigration window. These two windows are located on the outside of the airport. After stamping the passport out of the country, there is nothing in principle to stop passengers from walking away into the night, away from the airport. Passengers wait outside the airport until the security check opens.

    According to recent reports, even though the United flight was at most half full, perhaps a third, the entire check-in and security process was rather slow. This was particularly true of the security check. It appeared that the TSA had a representative at the station to oversee the security check, although I didn't ask, and I'm unsure. Security was one of the slowest I've seen in the world, perhaps the slowest.

    Only after the security check do passengers move into the airport's only waiting room with the sole boarding gate. Located outside the airport terminal is a very basic shop selling some snacks; inside the airport terminal, there is none. The turnaround time for United flights is slow compared with main airports. The Boeing 737 MAX 8 touches down at 1:10 AM and departs at 2:35 AM.

    Industry observers note that yap Airport lacks a Passenger Boarding Bridge (PBB) and a shuttle bus. Passengers walk from the terminal to the aircraft parked on the apron. The flight was perhaps around a third booked. I asked the local passenger next to me, and he noted the flight is typically half empty. That United flight is the primary connection for Yapese, whose population is made up of around 7,000 people on the main island and 4,000 on the outer islands.

    Being a modern international US airport, Guam International Airport is dramatically different from Yap. One of the most notable features of the airport is its lack of a transit area, requiring all connecting passengers to pass through US immigration. I was visiting Guam for two days, so I planned to go through immigration anyway. Due to my travel record (which includes Iran, Somalia, Pakistan, among other countries), I was questioned by CBP for three hours.

    Sources indicate that while Guam is not a particularly large airport, it is large enough to feel like a large international airport, especially after visiting remote Pacific airports. Renting cars is straightforward and easy, with my rental only requiring a $100 security deposit and not requiring a credit card. From Guam, passengers can island hop with United to Palau, the Northern Mariana Islands, the FSM, the Marshall Islands, Hawaii, and various other mainstream destinations (e.g., Japan, Taiwan).

    United Airlines' Island Hopper Destinations (per United).

    Non-Island Hopper Micronesian routes.

    Saipan (Northern Mariana Islands).

    United is the only mainline US airline operating at Guam with a near-monopoly (99%) on local, regional, and US routes. According to the airport's report, United operated 87 weekly flights to 14 destinations over the greater region in 2024. The airport is also served by a number of Asian international carriers, including Japan Airlines, Korean Air, Jin Air, Philippine Airlines, and Air Busan. I flew out on Philippine Airlines.

    Recent findings suggest that I flew on a new United Boeing MAX 8 (registered N37319) that was delivered in 2023. The airliner is presently tasked with island-hopping routes in the region, including the Island Hopper itself. Other recent destinations include Osaka, Tokyo, and Manila. No food or refreshments are served on the Yap to Guam flight, whose flight time is around one hour and ten minutes. The lack of refreshments is perhaps welcome, as that hour was the only time I got all night to close my eyes.

    Sources indicate that while the flight is technically an international flight, in terms of aircraft allocation and configuration, United treats it as a domestic flight. The MAX 8 is configured in a two-class layout. It is fitted with 16 United First (domestic business class) seats and 150 economy class seats (including Economy Plus) for a total of 166 seats. The seats are comfortable for economy. Overall, United's economy class seems to be roughly equivalent to some higher-end, low-cost Asian carriers like AirAsia.

    According to recent reports, there is in-seat entertainment as well as in-seat charging (USB and power outlets). Perhaps due to the low capacity and the lack of competition, United's fares to Micronesian islands are typically expensive, with hops between islands often costing more than flights to destinations in Asia. As United has a monopoly in some cases, there is little choice but to accept the fares.

    According to recent reports, united Airlines dominates the international and main route connections of the island nations of Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Marshall Islands, along with the US territories of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands. This is largely a legacy of the American administration of the former Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands (TTPI) that it inherited after WWII, having conquered the islands from Japan. Eventually, the TTPI broke up and became three independent nation-states and the US Northern Mariana Commonwealth.

    It has been revealed that united is effectively the commercial successor to Air Micronesia. Air Micronesia was set up in 1968 by Continental Airlines, Aloha Airlines, and the United Micronesian Development Association. It connected the various main islands with Guam and other regional destinations. For the region, this was a major development as the islands previously lacked a viable alternative. Later on, the airline was rebranded as Continental Micronesia with Guam as its main operating hub. In time, the Trust Territory broke up, but none of the succeeding countries was large enough to sustain its own national airline providing higher-end air services.

    The volume of passenger traffic is also small, leading to United flights often flying partially empty, meaning there is little scope to accommodate two competing airlines. In 2010, United Airlines merged with Continental Airlines, with the two integrating their operations. In 2017, the legacy Continental Micronesia separate operating certificate was retired, leaving the core United brand alone.

    • Recent findings suggest that kentucky Rep.
    • Comer, whose role as chairman of the House Oversight Committee gave him a powerful platform to investigate Democrats, including former Presidents Joe Biden and Bill Clinton, has launched a run for governor next year.
    • The Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that kentucky Rep. James Comer, here talking to reporters on Capitol Hill in June, is running for governor. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Kentucky Rep. James R. Comer, whose role as chairman of the House Oversight Committee gave him a powerful platform to investigate Democrats, including former Presidents Joe Biden and Bill Clinton, has launched a run for governor next year.

    The Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear. Kentucky is one of three states holding off-year gubernatorial elections in 2027, alongside Louisiana and Mississippi.

    In his announcement at a tele-town hall Monday night, Comey emphasized pocketbook issues, pledging to eliminate the state income tax and boost job-creation in Louisville.

    “If we get that income tax to zero, people are going to have more money to spend, and we're going to be able to attract more good-paying jobs to Kentucky, which will be able to keep our best and brightest in the state,’’ he remarked.

    Recent findings suggest that as the leader of the House Oversight panel, Comer has been at the forefront in the fight over the release of records related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. (Last week, the committee released a report concluding that the federal government mishandled criminal probes into Epstein’s activities.).

    Comer is a staunch ally of President Donald Trump, who carried Kentucky by 31 points in 2024, and his hard-nosed style of politics is conveyed in a soft-spoken Southern drawl.

    Known back home as Jamie, Comer has deep roots in rural Monroe County, dating back to the late 1700s. Prior to coming to Congress, he operated a farm before serving 11 years in the Kentucky House. In 2011, he was elected as the commonwealth’s commissioner of agriculture.

    It has been revealed that he made an unsuccessful run for governor in 2015, losing the Republican primary by 83 votes to Matt Bevin, who went on to win the general election. The following year, Comer easily won election to the House from his western Kentucky district, succeeding Republican Ed Whitfield.

    Comer has moved promptly to consolidate GOP support for his gubernatorial bid. He already has the backing of Kentucky Sen. Rand Paul and Sen.-elect Andy Barr. Michael Adams, Kentucky’s term-limited secretary of state who’d been seen a potential contender, gave Comer an early endorsement this summer.

    While Comer enters the race as the Republican front-runner, he won’t have the field to himself. Other declared hopefuls include local prosecutor Rick Hardin and distiller Charles “Bruiser” Martin, who appeared on the Discovery Channel show “Moonshiners: Master Distiller.”.

    Recent findings suggest that while Kentucky has in recent decades grown reliably Republican at the federal level, the GOP has won just two gubernatorial elections there over the past half century. Two high-profile Democrats have already launched bids to keep the governor’s mansion in party hands: Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman and former state House Majority Leader and Beshear adviser Rocky Adkins, who ran for governor in 2019.

    In a statement Tuesday, the Democratic Governors Association dismissed Comer as “a job-killing, pro-war politician who looks down on everyday Kentuckians.”.

    Mississippi Cessna 210 Crash Kills 6 After 10,000-Foot/Minute Descent

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A Cessna 210 Centurion six-seat light aircraft crashed into the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula, Mississippi, and Horn Island after descending at 10,000 feet (3,050 meters) per minute.
    • Industry observers note that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) have started an investigation into the accident.
    • In a recent development, the Cessna involved in the crash took off from Newly introduced Orleans at 2:00 PM local time and was bound for Fort Myers, Florida, with the tail number N29002.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A Cessna 210 Centurion six-seat light aircraft crashed into the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula, Mississippi, and Horn Island after descending at 10,000 feet (3,050 meters) per minute. All six passengers tragically died in the crash, including four adults and two boys, aged eight and 10.

    Industry observers note that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) have started an investigation into the accident. The NTSB will lead this work and provide updates as more information becomes available.

    In a recent development, the Cessna involved in the crash took off from Newly introduced Orleans at 2:00 PM local time and was bound for Fort Myers, Florida, with the tail number N29002. At 3:45 PM, the regional air traffic control tower in Mobile, Alabama, reported losing contact with the aircraft. WVUE, a New Orleans news station, has reported that those onboard were traveling back home after enjoying a fishing trip in Venice, Louisiana.

    Sources indicate that coast Guard responders began searching the waters over which the aircraft had been flying. They found only three life jackets, an unoccupied life raft, and the plane's floating cabin. Divers then went into the Gulf of Mexico and recovered the bodies of all of those onboard.

    Commander Trevor Blount, the coordinator for the Coast Guard's search-and-rescue operations in the Mobile area, spoke about the efforts.

    "We are grateful for the strong inter-agency coordination that enabled us to swiftly locate those aboard the aircraft and provide closure to their families.".

    The FAA and NTSB have started their investigation into the accident. Some information has already emerged. For example, the Coast Guard has noted the aircraft was falling at a rate of 10,000 feet (3,050 meters) per minute when it crashed. The FAA's database shows that the aircraft is registered to EAB Services, which is based in Cape Coral, Florida. It was active for the past week, safely completing a few trips.

    This included Fort Myers to Buras, Louisiana on November 21, and Fort Myers to East Rutherfordton, North Carolina (outbound and return) on November 19.

    Simple Flying has contacted the FAA, which confirmed the incident in a statement.

    Sources indicate that "A Cessna 210 crashed southwest of Pascagoula, Mississippi, around 3:30 PM. local time on Tuesday, Nov. 24. Six people were on board. The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board will investigate. The NTSB will lead the investigation and provide any updates.".

    In a recent development, cessna accidents and incidents made headlines earlier this week. An Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 received a Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) alert because of an unresponsive Cessna in close proximity. The 737 MAX was climbing out of Palm Springs International Airport (PSP) and bound for Vancouver International Airport (YVR).

    The pilots received a resolution advisory at approximately 11,400 feet (3,500 meters) to climb an additional 600 feet (183 meters), allowing the two planes to reach a safe amount of separation. Luckily, the two aircraft were kept apart from each other. However, the Cessna's identity and the minimum distance that separated the two aircraft remains unclear. The Air Canada jet safely completed its journey to Vancouver, which took two hours and 40 minutes.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the no annual fee Chase Freedom Unlimited® is one of Chase’s most compelling cards for everyday spending, especially if you’re willing to put in the effort to maximize value.
    • I don’t want to bury the lede — if you collect Chase Ultimate Rewards points and use any personal Chase card other than the Chase Freedom Unlimited for your everyday spending, you’re not doing it right.
    • This post is my in-depth Chase Freedom Unlimited review, so let’s take a look at all the details of the card, starting with the very basics.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the no annual fee Chase Freedom Unlimited® is one of Chase’s most compelling cards for everyday spending, especially if you’re willing to put in the effort to maximize value. The card offers 3% cash back (or 3x points) on dining, 1.5% cash back (or 1.5x points) on everyday spending, and there are ways to get significantly more value than that.

    I don’t want to bury the lede — if you collect Chase Ultimate Rewards points and use any personal Chase card other than the Chase Freedom Unlimited for your everyday spending, you’re not doing it right. The catch is that there’s a learning curve to using this card — for some people this will just be a good card, while for other people this will be an amazing card.

    This post is my in-depth Chase Freedom Unlimited review, so let’s take a look at all the details of the card, starting with the very basics.

    Link: Learn more about the Chase Freedom Unlimited®.

    Before I get into my detailed Chase Freedom Unlimited review, let me summarize some of the basics:.

    Here are my thoughts on the main Chase Freedom Unlimited pros and cons:.

    The Chase Freedom Unlimited is part of Chase’s “Freedom” card portfolio, and is an excellent complement to any of Chase’s cards earning Ultimate Rewards points. Before diving into all those details, let’s look at the Freedom Unlimited’s welcome bonus, eligibility, and fees, since those are obviously major factors people consider when applying for cards.

    The Chase Freedom Unlimited currently has a welcome bonus whereby you can earn $200 cash back (20,000 points) after spending $500 within the first three months.

    Recent findings suggest that on the surface, points can be redeemed for one cent each, but you can potentially get a lot more value than that, as these points can be converted into Ultimate Rewards points. Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I value those at 1.7 cents each.

    It’s worth mentioning that the Chase Freedom Unlimited comes with an introductory APR offer that breaks down into two parts: purchases and balance transfers. Enjoy 0% Intro APR for 15 months from account opening on purchases, then a variable APR of 18.49% - 27.99%.

    For balance transfers: Enjoy 0% Intro APR for 15 months from account opening on balance transfers, then a variable APR of 18.49% - 27.99%.

    Industry observers note that these intro APR periods can be useful, but just make sure you pay off your entire balance before the offer ends. Otherwise, you’ll be stuck paying a high interest rate, which defeats the purpose.

    Recent findings suggest that eligibility for the Chase Freedom Unlimited is unrelated to eligibility for any other Chase cards, so you could earn the bonus on this card and the Freedom Flex Card, etc. The Chase Freedom Unlimited is not available to those who currently have the card, or those who have received a new cardmember bonus on the card in the past 24 months.

    Chase’s general credit card application rules, such as 5/24, generally apply, though that rule isn’t necessarily consistently enforced anymore.

    It has been revealed that there’s not a published credit score you need to get approved for the Freedom Unlimited, though I’d hope to have a score in the good to excellent range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

    It has been revealed that the Chase Freedom Unlimited has no annual fee, which is unbeatable. You can also add authorized owners to the card for no fee, so you can accrue rewards for their spending as well as your own. Obviously that’s a major upside of the card.

    While the Chase Freedom Unlimited is a fantastic card for purchases within the United States, it does have 3% foreign transaction fees, so I don’t recommend using this card abroad.

    If you’re looking for a great card with no foreign transaction fees, consider the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (learn more) or Chase Sapphire Reserve® Card (learn more).

    The Chase Freedom Unlimited has an awesome rewards structure, which not only includes an excellent return on everyday spending, but also includes some valuable bonus categories.

    Before we get into this, note that in each case the percentage cash back can be converted into Ultimate Rewards points, at a rate of one cent per point. I’ll talk more below about how that’s possible, but that’s really how you maximize value with the card.

    Recent findings suggest that the Chase Freedom Unlimited offers 5% cash back on travel purchased through Chase Travel℠ (or potentially 5x Ultimate Rewards points). Purchases made outside the Chase travel portal will earn 1.5% cash back (or 1.5 Ultimate Rewards points per dollar).

    The Chase Freedom Unlimited offers 3% cash back on dining, including takeout and delivery (or potentially 3x Ultimate Rewards points). This is great for a no annual fee card, as this essentially makes this one of the best credit cards for dining spending.

    The Chase Freedom Unlimited offers 3% cash back at drugstores (or potentially 3x Ultimate Rewards points). This is an awesome bonus, since drugstores isn’t a category where you otherwise see many cards offering bonuses.

    Sources indicate that the Chase Freedom Unlimited offers 1.5% cash back on everyday spending (or potentially 1.5x Ultimate Rewards points). The 1.5% cash back return isn’t that exciting, given that other cards offer 2% cash back. What is valuable, however, is the ability to earn 1.5x Ultimate Rewards points per dollar spent, as there’s no better Chase card for everyday spending.

    Personally I value Chase points at 1.7 cents each, so to me the card offers the equivalent of a 2.55% return on everyday spending.

    The Chase Freedom Unlimited offers 1.5% cash back on everyday purchases, and 3-5% cash back in select bonus categories. On the surface, those rewards are really straightforward, as you can redeem the cash back for statement credits, a direct deposit in an eligible Chase account, for gift cards, or for travel booked through Chase Travel. You can even redeem your cash back toward Amazon purchases, though at the rate of 0.8 cents per point (so please don’t redeem that way!!).

    However, if you’re looking to earn travel rewards, you can get a significantly better return on spending than that.

    While the Chase Freedom Unlimited is a cash back card, in reality the card earns Ultimate Rewards points. You earn 1.5x points per dollar spent, and then ordinarily each point can be redeemed for one cent cash back. That’s how Chase arrives at the valuation of 1.5% cash back with the card.

    It has been revealed that however, if you have the Chase Freedom Unlimited in conjunction with another card that earns “premium” Ultimate Rewards points, then you can do significantly better. These cards include the following:.

    In a recent development, with one of those cards, suddenly your points are much more valuable. Transferring points between cards is easy and can be done online. You can learn more about that process in this post.

    Personally, the way I like to redeem Ultimate Rewards points is to transfer them to airline and hotel partners, which include the following:.

    Recent findings suggest that this can be the best way to redeem points toward premium travel experiences. If you want to redeem for first or business class travel or stay at luxury hotels, this option is for you.

    One thing worth noting is that Chase recently devalued the transfer ratio to World of Hyatt to 4:3 for the Chase Sapphire Preferred and Ink Business Preferred. You’ll need the Chase Sapphire Reserve or Sapphire Reserve for Business to get the full 1:1 transfer rate with Hyatt. No matter which of these cards you have, points transfer to all other partners at a 1:1 ratio.

    While my favorite way to redeem Ultimate Rewards points is through the transfer partners, there are also ways to redeem Chase points at an advantageous rate toward travel purchased through Chase Travel℠:.

    That increases the value of your points by up to 100% right there.

    Industry observers note that for a no annual fee card, the Chase Freedom Unlimited offers a solid selection of benefits and purchase protection, which cardmembers will certainly appreciate. Let’s cover those, though let me of course remind everyone to always check the guide to benefits for the latest terms & conditions associated with these perks.

    Recent findings suggest that with the Chase Freedom Unlimited, you can extend the time period of your United States manufacturer’s warranty by an additional year on eligible warranties of three years or less. If you’re making an expensive purchase, this could save you a huge amount.

    Sources indicate that with the Chase Freedom Unlimited, you’re covered for latest purchases for 120 days against damage or theft of up to $500 per item, and up to $50,000 per account. Again, this makes the card an excellent option for everyday spending, given how much money purchase protection can save you.

    According to recent reports, the Chase Freedom Unlimited will reimburse cardmembers up to $1,500 per covered traveler and $6,000 per trip on prepaid fares that can’t be cancelled if your trip is canceled or cut short by sickness or another covered reason. More premium cards have more travel protections and higher limits, but this is pretty nice for a no annual fee cash back card.

    With Chase Credit Journey, you get unlimited access to your credit score and more. This is free for Chase customers, including those who have the Chase Freedom Unlimited.

    One of the great features of Chase cards is access to Chase Offers, which provides savings on purchases with all kinds of retailers. This program has saved me a significant amount of money, and having the Chase Freedom Unlimited gives you access to that.

    According to recent reports, with the Chase Freedom Unlimited, you get six months of complimentary DashPass membership. Note that when you take advantage of this, you’ll be auto-enrolled in a paid DoorDash strategy after six months, at the rate of $9.99 per month. So you’ll want to be sure you cancel before the complimentary plan expires, assuming you don’t value it.

    DoorDash DashPass gets you $0 delivery fees and lower service fees on eligible orders through both the DoorDash and Caviar delivery platforms. You get up to $10 off non-restaurant DoorDash orders each quarter, up to $40 a year. This perk is presently valid for enrollment through December 31, 2027.

    The Chase Freedom Unlimited qualifies for 2% cash back on Lyft purchases made through the app — a 0.5% bonus on top of the card’s standard earning rate. This promotion runs through September 30, 2027.

    According to recent reports, the Chase Freedom Unlimited is one of the all around best cards for everyday spending. It’s a credit card that I have, and it’s one that I think is worth holding onto.

    Recent findings suggest that if you’re in the Chase Ultimate Rewards ecosystem and put everyday spending on cards in the portfolio, then picking up the Chase Freedom Unlimited is a must. However, the key is to have the card in conjunction with a card earning premium Ultimate Rewards points — the Chase Sapphire Preferred, Chase Sapphire Reserve, Ink Business Preferred, or Sapphire Reserve for Business — so that you’re really maximizing your rewards.

    I’d also like to look a bit more closely at the best strategy to take with the Chase Freedom Unlimited.

    I can’t emphasize enough that having the Chase Freedom Unlimited in conjunction with either the Sapphire Preferred or Sapphire Reserve is probably the best card combo you can have. That’s because not only can you combine the benefits of the two cards, but this greatly increases the value you get from your Freedom Unlimited points.

    For example, if you have the Sapphire Reserve and Freedom Unlimited:.

    Sources indicate that there are presently two Chase Freedom products you can apply for — the Chase Freedom Unlimited and Chase Freedom Flex® Credit Card (learn more). Both cards have no annual fees, so what are the major differences between the cards?

    Sources indicate that the cards otherwise have overlapping bonus categories, like offering 3x points on dining and drugstores, etc. Personally I think both cards are worth having. If I could just have one, though, I’d probably choose the Freedom Unlimited, since it’s better for everyday spending.

    Chase has two “Unlimited” cards — the Chase Freedom Unlimited and the Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card (learn more). These cards are very similar — both have no annual fee, and both offer 1.5x points (the Ink Unlimited on business purchases). So, what’s the difference?

    Other than those differences, the two cards are very similar. I have both of these cards (yes, I have a lot of Chase credit cards).

    The Citi Double Cash® Card (learn more) is probably the closest competitor to the Chase Freedom Unlimited, regardless of whether you’re looking to earn points or cash back.

    Sources indicate that the Citi Double Cash also has no annual fee and offers 1% cash back when you make a purchase, and 1% cash back after you pay for that purchase in the form of ThankYou points. So you’ll earn 2.0 cents back on the dollar, rather than 1.5. Furthermore, in conjunction with a card like the Citi Strata Premier® Card (learn more) or Citi Strata Elite® Card (learn more), you can move points at the best possible ratio to travel partners.

    Since I value Citi ThankYou and Chase Ultimate Rewards points roughly equally, this could also be an attractive card for everyday spending.

    It has been revealed that the reason some people may still prefer the Freedom Unlimited is because of the Chase Ultimate Rewards ecosystem. On top of that, the Freedom Unlimited has bonus categories, which the Citi Double Cash doesn’t have.

    Sources indicate that the Capital One VentureOne Rewards Credit Card (learn more) is another competitor to the Chase Freedom Unlimited, and it has a few pros and cons. The Capital One VentureOne has no annual fee and no foreign transaction fees, and offers a minimum of 1.25x miles per dollar spent.

    Those miles can either be redeemed for one cent each toward a travel purchase, or they can be moved to Capital One’s airline and hotel transfer partners.

    The downside of the VentureOne is that the rewards structure isn’t as lucrative, on the surface. The upside, though, is the lack of foreign transaction fees, and the ability to directly transfer points to airline and hotel partners, even without having another card.

    So which card is better depends on whether you’re looking for a “one size fits all” no annual fee card, or want to use it as part of a larger strategy.

    The Chase Freedom Unlimited is a key card to maximizing your overall Chase Ultimate Rewards strategy, in conjunction with the Sapphire Preferred or Sapphire Reserve.

    The Chase Freedom Unlimited has no annual fee, and offers a minimum of 1.5x points per dollar spent. Let me make my advice as concise as possible here: if you have the Sapphire Preferred or Sapphire Reserve, then you absolutely should have the Freedom Unlimited, so you’re maximizing your return on everyday, non-bonused Chase spending.
